text: Erin Solstice is a twenty-year-old woman from Michigan who likes strategy games such as chess, shogi and go.
Erin reaches this world by accident: she only wanted to go to the bathroom and instead found herself looking down the snout of a dragon.
In the first chapter a burned and bleeding Erin finds a long-deserted inn built of oak boards on a stone foundation, about four times the size of a normal house.
Cleaning the inn's common room gives Erin the [Innkeeper] class at Level 1 with the Skills Basic Cleaning and Basic Cooking.
Erin concludes that the world works like a video game, with levels and Skills announced as thoughts in her head.
The inn stands on a long, gradual incline of the grassland, and Liscor can be seen in the distance from it.
Erin estimates the walk from the inn to Liscor at about an hour, although Relc and Klbkch had called it ten minutes.
The inn was once part of a small community that died of a plague, and no law forbids occupying the site.
Relc, a Drake in the city watch, and Klbkch, an Antinium Senior Guardsman, come to the inn after smoke is spotted from Liscor's walls and the Captain sends someone to check.
Erin paints the new name "The Wandering Inn" on the inn's plaque and hammers a sign into the ground beside it reading "No Killing Goblins".
Goblins chase Erin toward the inn, and when Klbkch offers to dispose of the Goblins still hiding nearby she refuses, saying "No killing Goblins" and that it is wrong.

While Erin sleeps in her inn, a spell completed by a chanting man before onlookers summons young Humans who appear mid-motion, many looking up from smartphones, and who are then shown turning up in several places.
The summoned Humans are not legends and have no special powers beyond those all Humans have.
Ryoka Griffin, a barefoot Runner who knows she is in another world with no way back, is introduced as a second Earth arrival.
Erin plays and beats the Drake Olesm at chess on a wager set by a shopkeeper she says ripped her off, and Klbkch hands her three gold coins and some copper and silver as her wager.
The Antinium Queen allows twelve Workers to visit the inn, where Erin teaches them and a Goblin group to play chess.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Ryoka lists the continents as Baleros, the Blighted Kingdoms of Rhir, Terandria, Chandrar, and Izril.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Ryoka's reading confirms five main continents - Rhir, Izril, Terandria, Chandrar and Baleros - and that Humans live on all of them in some form.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Baleros is described as a mysterious continent of jungles and Gazers.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: The Blighted Kingdoms of Rhir are described as dying lands locked in eternal conflict.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Terandria is described as a kingdom-continent of knights, royalty and Humans.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Chandrar is the home of the King of Destruction and holds a desert larger than the United States.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: The Drakes call the home continent Issrysil, while Ryoka prefers the name Izril.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Selys, drawing a map for Erin, calls the continent "Semariss" and says Humans have another name for it.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Ryoka's reading shows a world far larger than Earth, where nations the size of the United States or Russia count as normal or small.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Ryoka concludes that war dominates the history she reads, and that large empires fail because of supply, death of the ruler, rising high-level individuals and dependence on magic.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: Other peoples named in Ryoka's reading as powers: the Slave Traders of Roshal on Chandrar, about as powerful as Wistram but neutral.

section: The world at a glance: continents
text: The Minotaurs hold an archipelago and have tried to take over the world several times.

On Selys's map the Humans of Izril live across the northern part of the continent up to where the mountains start, and a long line of mountains drawn two thirds up nearly cuts the top third off from the bottom.
Liscor sits near the middle where the continent narrows, and is one of the few ways through the mountains besides the High Passes and the coastal routes.
The High Passes are unsafe even for high-level adventurers because of nasty creatures living there.
The south of Izril is home to Drakes, Gnolls and Antinium, with a few other races.
Selys marks six known Antinium colonies in the south; the ones other than Liscor's are described as hostile.
The big southern groupings are the Walled Cities, the Gnoll Tribes of the plains, and the independent ports and cities.
Nearly a third of the southern population are Harpies and Naga according to Selys, with some Minotaurs coming and going.
The southern cities fight constantly, and Liscor's army is usually hired out on campaign elsewhere.
There are six Walled Cities, and Pallass is the northernmost of them.
The Walled Cities named in a joint call during the Face-Eater Moth crisis are Zeres, Pallass, Salazsar, Manus, Fissival and Oteslia.
The Walled Cities differ in government: some elect an official, some are run by a body of powerful individuals and some by a hereditary leader.
Pisces tells the inn that the Walled Cities were meant to defend from Dragons and that the Drakes set the skeletons of their ancestors into the walls.
A Walled City's nobles include Wall Lords or Lords of the Wall, as in Wall Lord Ilvriss.
The Five Families of the human north - Reinhart, Veltras, Terland, Wellfar and El - were the first Humans to settle on Izril, are related to Terandrian kings, and remain rich and influential.

First Landing is called the first and grandest of the Human cities built on Izril, a walled metropolis watching the north sea, built by Human nobility who fled Terandria; Magnolia Reinhart's carriage stops there before a large mansion.
Lady Magnolia Reinhart is the heir to the Reinhart family and one of the richest people on the continent.
Fals says Invrisil, the city of adventurers, is a large city far to the north, six hundred miles from where he and Ryoka are talking.
Riverfarm is a village with no ruler but its village head, in the early days.
Selys says Liscor's Antinium have some sort of bargain with all the southern cities: they will not fight and have no army.
Klbkch says that under Liscorian law Goblins are considered monsters and bandits for the purposes of determining crime.
Krshia says Wistram is no friend to the magicless and that Gnolls will not deal with it, a grudge dating from a gathering of the Gnoll tribes nearly twenty years earlier.
Erin estimates that Humans are rare among Liscor's crowds, perhaps one for every forty nonhumans, in her early days.
On Erin's first visit to Liscor's Adventurer's Guild, a Gnoll and the Drakes glare at each other so tensely that Erin expects the room to explode if either side moves.
Klbkch says it is said that the three most dangerous things to Liscor are rain, the undead and war.
Watch Captain Zevara leads Liscor's City Watch.
Klbkch cites an agreement with Liscor under which the Antinium may bring Soldiers above ground unless requested by a figure of authority or in times of war or defence of the city.
Xrn tells Klbkch that in over two decades since the Antinium reached Izril, no new Queens have been born.
Ryoka's reading places the Dwarves on Terandria, although they once lived everywhere.
Lyonette's narrated thoughts name her as a scion of the Marquin house, one of the Hundred Families of Terrandria, and Sixth Princess in line to the Eternal Throne of Calanfer.
Calanfer's throne is called eternal but dates back about six thousand years, according to Lyonette.
In the north of Terandria the nation of Ailendamus is described as thrice the size of Calanfer, Gaiil-Drome and Kaliv put together.
Calanfer, Gaiil-Drome and Kaliv held off Ailendamus and six other nations in the last war, Petril's Folly, twenty-eight years earlier.
Kaliv is a high-altitude nation of Humans whose rulers are Griffin Kings or Queens.
On Baleros much of the fighting is done by mercenary groups, from small troops to huge Companies, and the Companies have their own cities and act like nations.
Geneva has heard the Four Companies of Baleros are the biggest, and the soldier Fortum says that if two of the Great Companies fought, the other two would attack the winner.
One of the Four Great Companies is the Armored Legion, which is largely Dullahan and based mainly in the north.
Niers Astoragon is second in command of one of the Four Great Companies and the highest-leveled [Strategist] on the continent, nicknamed the Titan.
Niers is a Fraerling, a people about as tall as a Human's hand who are reclusive on Baleros.
Chandrar is an arid continent, with heat by day and cold by night in many regions, and a vast desert at its centre that cuts off civilization for thousands of miles.
The nations of Chandrar border the great central desert rather than lying within it.
Reim, home of Flos, lies in the northeast of Chandrar and borders the great desert, which makes it dry.
Germina is one of four remaining Shield Kingdoms, its capital Ger sits on an oasis, and its ruler bears the title Quarass.
Hellios, northeast of Germina, is ruled by Queen Calliope; its [King] Treland died decades earlier at Flos' hands in his first wars of expansion.
To the north lie the Republic of Belchan, which elects a [Prime Minister], and the Realm of Jecrass, which has a [King].
West of Reim lies Khelt, a land whose army is undead, led by King Fetohep.
The Empire of Sands is the newest power on Chandrar, claiming the western civilizations across the great desert under a new [Emperor], and is hostile to Flos.
South of Reim lies Nerrhavia's Fall, a once-great empire of String People overthrown by the kingdom that now bears the name.
Tiqr, a Garuda-populated land with war elephants, is the one nation Flos expects might ally with him.
Flos names Pomle, Savere and Illivere as dangerous nations; Pomle, tiny and shaped like a circle, is not hostile to Reim.
The Thalassocracy of Medain is a nation of adventurers with three vast magical dungeons.
Flos conquered nearly all of Chandrar and landed armies on Izril's southern shores before he vanished.
Flos says the Traders of Roshal are an independent third party to whom he sold the prisoners taken in the battle for Reim, and who may ransom those with wealth.
Rhir is a continent under constant war, ruled by the Blighted King, who fights monster tribes and demons.
The heart of the kingdom is the shield city of Paranfer, whose four great walls have stood for thousands of years.
Rhir is at war with a Demon King, leader of the continent's Demons and monsters.
The Antinium came from Rhir, arriving on Izril in four small ships in the last month of winter.
Rhir has no Assassin's Guild, since infighting of that kind would be too harmful.
Ryoka's reading finds Rhir is always at war with some threat or other, and that the Demons emerged five thousand years back.
Wistram is the Isle of Mages, where at least three archmages have their homes.
New Wistram students are taken once a year; a month costs twenty gold and an exam decides who may stay free.
During the Face-Eater Moth call, Wistram says it will amplify a Scrying spell to all interested parties and that its mages are ready to link.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Relc says Drakes are distantly related to dragons and can breathe fire, and that being taken for lizardfolk is wrong and rude.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Selys says most of the inhabitants of southern Izril are Drakes, alongside Gnolls, Antinium and other races.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Gnolls live in tribes on the plains of southern Izril, and the tribes gather to talk and form alliances every ten years.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Beastkin come from another continent further south and are mostly found among the Gnoll tribes.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: In 5 B.F. the news from Rhir was of a new species dubbed the 'Antinium', who then vanished from that continent.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Pawn tells Erin that the hundred Antinium gathered play chess against her as one mind, seeing a hundred moves and playing them in turn.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Goblins are small, wiry, with pointed ears, two rows of shark-like teeth and blood-red eyes, and they scream as they chase.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Ryoka reflects that Goblins always come back no matter how many times they get wiped out, and that there are reports of what happens when a Goblin King emerges.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Ceria tells Erin she is a Half-elf, not an Elf, and that no one has seen an Elf for thousands of years because they all died long ago.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Dullahans are covered in armor except for the head, and the quality of the armor varies.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Jelaqua, a Selphid, says "parasites" is a good word for Selphids: they are thieves who steal bodies, the only way they can live.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: The Garuda are bird-people native to Chandrar.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Fraerlings, or the Small Folk, are a Baleros people about as tall as a Human's hand.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: The leader of the adventuring group the Horns of Hammerad is a minotaur [Fighter], and Ryoka's reading says the Minotaurs have an archipelago.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: The String People of Chandrar once formed a single empire that unified about six thousand years earlier.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Ryoka's reading says the Dragons are mostly dead, with one slain every few thousand years, and Relc says Drakes are related to Dragons.

section: The main peoples at a glance
text: Frost Faeries are treated by Liscor's people as a force of nature rather than as creatures.
Coins in common use are gold, silver, copper and bronze.
A silver coin is ten copper and a gold coin is twenty silver.
The average worker earns about three or four silver coins a day.
One gold coin is a lot for villagers; every family might have one gold coin's worth in savings.
Erin's first purchase, a bag of flour, oil, butter, four sausages, two onions and sugar, salt and yeast, is priced at three gold and eight silver.
A bathhouse in Liscor costs five copper for Drakes, with Gnolls and other furred Beastkin paying double.
Years are counted in A.F.; Durene, a villager of Riverfarm, thinks the current year is around 22 A.F.
The book on the Second Antinium War opens in the year 13 A.F., with Izril tentatively at peace.
Ryoka finds that many old books date events by an event-based system rather than a numbered calendar.
Rhir has its own calendar, with years named in numbers and names such as 2118 Zekol.
The Antinium of Liscor's Hive do not go aboveground in the first two months of spring.
Ryoka remembers that the Winter Solstice is the shortest day of the year, and Ivolethe says winter is two-thirds done and that the shortest day marks the beginning of the end.
The Winter Solstice stands as close to a new year as this world has, in Erin's view.

Maran and Agnes tell Erin that the city's festival days offer candied apples, games and city-bought entertainments, that the Winter Solstice is coming and always a good time, and that it is a romantic time.
A sand hourglass is used to time the twenty minutes until dinner in an Earther company's camp.
Runners deliver quickly, and merchants, caravans and ship captains also carry letters between cities and continents for a few coppers.
Letters change hands like currency, so a letter to another continent can cost a copper coin or two and take a month or two.
Couriers are rare long-distance specialists, fewer than a hundred on the continent, running around a thousand miles on a delivery.
Adventurers send [Message] spells through the local Mage's Guild, which hands the request to the Runner's Guild for delivery.
Lady Magnolia hands the delivering Runner a seal, a token half gleaming silver and half semi-translucent cerulean.
Ryoka says the Runner's Guild has bags of holding and bets that, if you had the coin, someone could be in Riverfarm, thirty miles off, within the hour.
During the Face-Eater Moth crisis the Walled Cities set up a group [Message] call under established emergency protocol.
Pisces affixes an anchoring spell to an actual door and harnesses the teleportation spell to create a portal rather than just transport people.
The door drinks a great deal of mana, and once spent takes a long time to recharge.
Pisces and Moore report the door can send someone of Ryoka's general weight 536 miles under minimal change in altitude or magical ambience, and then needs roughly 8.2 hours to recharge fully.
Fals says First Landing, the port city, is the largest city on his side of the continent, and over three thousand miles north of where they stand, closer to four thousand than not.
Television arrives in the world as magicvision, a new technology colored by influence from Earth.
The Unmarked Coach is a hard-to-request, fast transport counterpart to Magnolia Reinhart's pink carriage.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: Most adventuring ranking systems top out at Gold-rank, with Bronze and Silver below; adventurers whose renown goes beyond that are no longer ranked but are called Named adventurers.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: The top Gold-rank teams are equivalent to small armies, while a Bronze-rank team is not much better than a group of rookies.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: The Merchant's Guild handles mundane traffic by caravan and is a rival to the Runner's Guild, slower but cheaper for goods with protection.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: The Mage's Guild carries [Message] spells and told Erin it would not allow her door to take over messages between Liscor and Celum.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: A speaker warns Ryoka that the Assassin's Guild in Izril is quite competent, and calls Liscor's army its de facto governing body.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: Guilds are powerful in cities but Lords hold their own standing forces, and Guilds pick their battles rarely, hiring mercenaries or fighting as the Adventurer's and Runner's Guilds do.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: Reynold says even a [Shopkeeper] can sell a [Lord], meaning merchants have political influence.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: Reynold says the [Lords] and [Ladies] of the Five Families maneuver with each other in the politics of the continent's major cities, and that he has heard the Drakes in the south play a far more direct and material version.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: Krshia says Wistram is nationless and a nation unto itself, and has never bowed to any ruler.

section: The big institutions at a glance
text: The Four Great Companies of Baleros are mercenary Companies that act like nations.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Klbkch explains that classes are general ways of life people take, that each new level raises proficiency at the role, and that skills may be learnt along the way.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: A new class is gained by meeting its requirements, which are often known but not always.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Relc says a man he knew gained four levels in [Farmer] just by growing carrots in pots beside his window.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Early on Erin says she kept levelling every time she fell asleep, and Relc asks whether the notification woke her as she fell asleep, saying he hates that and that it is very annoying.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Level-ups appear as bracketed lines, for example "[Innkeeper Level 11!]" followed by skill lines such as "[Skill – Lesser Strength Obtained!]".

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Narration from Rags's viewpoint says that in this world levelling up was more important than a birthday and an occasion for rejoicing, and her tribe celebrates after she tells them she has changed class.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Klbkch says only the thinking races can level, while animals and even Dragons cannot; Goblins can.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Klbkch says all races that think are given the ability to level and take classes, and that no one knows who set this up.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Klbkch recites a passage whose exact wording he says comes from The Book of Levels, originally written nearly a thousand years ago: all who Think Feel, from Feeling they Act, in Action they Level, all who Think have a Class, and in that Class they find destiny.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Klbkch tells the tale that once all races fought with tooth, claw and magic, and those who forsook their natures were given the gift of [Leveling] while the rest kept the might of their natures.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Erin's early conclusion is that the world works like a game, with levels and skills announced in her head.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Krshia says leveling comes from learning and trials, so doing the same thing without change gives no experience.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Selys says Erin has probably levelled so quickly because starting an inn by herself must be a lot harder than just working in one or taking over a business.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Erin says she gained ten levels in a month and is Level 10, and Selys says nobody levels that fast.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Selys says people normally apprentice for years before reaching Level 10 and most people of her age are barely Level 12 in their chosen profession.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: In-world, some people treat levelling as a religion and worship those with the highest levels.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Krshia has heard it said that each person is given a maximum level, and that reaching it means the end of their life.

section: Levelling: what it is and who does it
text: Ceria says some people claim everyone has a set amount of levels in them and will run out if they gain too many across different classes; Ryoka says she does not believe this either.
Krshia says the elderly people she has known have levels in their twenties or sometimes thirties, none above Level 40, and few reach their thirtieth level.
Krshia says only a few people in each continent are above Level 50, and she does not think she knows of anyone living above Level 70, only ancient legends of heroes at that level.
Klbkch says most people reach about Level 20 in one class, a few reach 30, those who reach 40 are famous, and those past 50 are known throughout the world.
Klbkch says there are a handful of Level 30s in each town and a few dozen in a city.
Klbkch knows of no one near Level 100, though legends tell of levels above eighty and ninety.
Klbkch says most people grow too old to keep levelling long before passing Level 60.

Ressa tells Lady Magnolia that, leaving out city-states' private armies and other lords' retainers, they can call upon two thousand individuals with combat-classes above Level 20, over six hundred of them above Level 30, six Named Adventurers, eight Gold-rank teams and at least three hundred and fifty irregular units.
Lyonette says her family keeps a list of rulers above Level 40 and that fewer than forty exist in the world, counting only [Kings] and [Queens].
Lyonette's father guessed the King of Destruction is probably just above Level 50 and not yet Level 60, among the highest-levelled [Kings] in the world.
Selys says Relc is about Level 32, which is incredibly different from a Level 13 [Warrior].
Garia says [Enhanced Strength] only comes to warrior classes around Level 30, so getting it so early means she is a lot stronger than normal.
Selys says Peslas, a Liscor [Innkeeper] above Level 30, runs one of the best inns in the city but, being old and relaxed, levels about once every couple of years.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Grimalkin says [Warriors] tend to gain a powerful Skill with their class around Level 30, in an offensive, defensive or utility direction.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Val agrees with Ryoka's guess that there are rare skills every ten levels and says he got his [Double Step] skill at Level 30.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Garia has heard that a [Greater Strength] skill exists for people of very high level but has never seen anyone with it.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: A Level 20 requirement is the entry to the Knights of the Petal and the prerequisite for the [Knight] class.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Calvaron tells two new Wistram students that unless they are over Level 20 or have some new spell or talent they will be hard-pressed to pass the exam, unless they have a patron to sponsor them.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: A man who comes up beside the narrator says Sir Richard, having reached Level 30 as a [Knight], is considered a peer of the realm in many respects, and that all those with a level higher than 30 are honored in various ways by the crown.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Liscor's Watch orders a curfew just past dark for anyone without ten levels in a combat class.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Calvaron tells new Wistram students that most magic classes require ten to twenty levels of [Mage] first, which is why schools teach basics.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Spell Tiers loosely follow caster level: up to about Level 16 for 1st or 0 Tier, about 24 for 2nd Tier, about 32 for 3rd Tier, though lower-level mages can cast higher Tier magic with practice.

section: Level thresholds and what they mean
text: Ilvriss says a [Strategist] is Level 30, or lower if one combines a military rank with [Tactician], though he calls the shortcut diluted.
Selys says levels can replace numbers and muscle only if there is a big difference in levels.
Magnolia says the Antinium fight assuming all soldiers are equal because they do not level, and that other armies fight differently.
Lyonette says a Level 60 [Mayor] might equal a Level 30 [King], because a [King]'s power extends across the whole kingdom.
Klbkch says that at his peak he was a Level 44 [Swordslayer] and Level 26 [Assassin] and Ryoka notes he was then stronger than a typical Named Adventurer.
Ryoka estimates a Named Adventurer is only around Level 40.
Cervial says Silver-rank is mostly the low twenties at best and Gold-rank starts around Level 24, though equipment and skill matter.
Grimalkin says Yvlon's sword already puts her at Gold-rank, and he will certify her Gold if she gains a decent Level 30 Skill.

After the battle, Dawil, the Horns, Moore, Seborn and Halrac raise their hands to say they levelled, while Revi scowls, Yvlon asks her brother, Falene and the others if they did not level, and Ylawes says he will probably level within the next week or month at the latest.
Ylawes says most of them are past Level 30, and Dawil says this lot does not level every time they go into a hairy situation before asking about Skills and saying he got nothing.
Lyonette says the better a class, the slower its holder levels; she adds that royalty also level slowly because they rarely face danger.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: A class announces itself with a message: Erin's first night gives "[Innkeeper Class Obtained!]", "[Innkeeper Level 1!]" and the skills [Basic Cleaning] and [Basic Cooking].

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Klbkch says that for some classes the requirements are known but there are exceptions, and a [Ruler]-type class cannot simply be taken; Erin guesses you must be born into it.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Krshia says only things people make their goals and dreams form classes, not everyday acts like walking, and a [Gourmet] class exists for some rich merchants and nobles.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Selys says a person can qualify for a class and still not get it, because it has to become part of their life.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Selys says need and want determine which skills people get, so people get them at different times or in different variations.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Pisces says Erin gains no [Tactician] levels from chess unless she considers its tactical applications, because chess gives far less experience than real work as a strategist.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Laken works out that his [Emperor] class and its level came from intent and purpose, and he reasons that exp for an [Emperor] involves growing his kingdom and gaining subjects.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Rags's early Goblin classes were Level 2 [Backstabber] and Level 5 [Scavenger].

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Selys says a [Spearmaster] who starts using a sword would get [Warrior] first, and later a specialised class such as [Swordslayer] or [Duelist] once level and skills allow.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Selys says classes change names mainly to show specialisation or higher level, and [Tactician] can become [Leader] or [General] or stay the same depending on skills.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Embria says a [Spearmaster] can be gained by years of training or by killing one in combat.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Class changes announce themselves with a line like "[Conditions Met: Innkeeper → Magical Innkeeper Class!]", as when Erin reaches Level 30 as an [Innkeeper].

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Klbkch says there is no one set of skills for a class, so two [Soldiers] may learn different skills at the same level.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Klbkch notes that while Relc is a higher-level [Guardsman] than he, Relc lacks the [Detect Guilt] skill.

section: What a class is and how one is gained
text: Garia says [Farm Workers] are looked down on, yet the class gives useful skills like [Lesser Strength], and she got it on her second level.
Flos tells the twins that many classes are narrow in purpose, so a [Farmer] cannot learn dancing skills but may learn to defend his land or lead helpers.

Flos says some classes have more opportunity and force: a [Survivor] has many Skills but a [Lord] will have more powerful Skills, and a [King] stands above all other classes as one of the few with the strongest Skills.
Lyonette says a [General] can affect whole armies and Skills like demoralising enemy armies, so classes that influence people are among the best.
Lyonette says royal, rare and merged classes are better than normal ones and a [Princess] can give someone a unique class.
Lyonette says a [Lord] has almost the Skills of a [General] but can also empower his estate, and a [Blademaster] has far better Skills than any [Warrior] or normal [Knight].
Lyonette says an [Emperor] may be better than a [King] because only the emperor's Skills affect the entire empire.
Laken believes [General], [Steward] and [Paladin] are rare and stronger than normal classes because they are more important.
Olesm calls [Tactician] the first of the strategist class line, which might lead to [Strategist] and then [Grandmaster].
Olesm says he has heard of people getting the [Layabout] or [Idler] class, which usually only applies to the aristocracy.
Drassi is a Level 17 [Gossip], a class most people have never heard of, with the Skills [Time to Chat] and [Trusted Voice].
The Earther narrator says a [Clown] might not exist in this world, but classes are what people make them.
A Level 1 [Hero] class was given to all the summoned Earthers, speeds levelling in other classes, and many later lost it.
Tom reports that some of the Earthers think the [Hero] class has only one level, and he reasons that a [Hero] is only a hero if other people think he is.
Numbtongue's [Bard] and Headscratcher's [Berserker] are called unique classes for Goblins, and the Hobs cannot think of any Goblin who had [Bard].
Viceria says some classes shape the way people look: [Mages] tend to be thin and look younger, while [Farmers] tend to grow larger, and Garia's first class was [Farmer].
Selys says in theory you could have as many classes as you want, but even most Adventurers have only three or four.
In an online chat among Earthers, a Level 12 Warrior says more classes mean more skills, while Loran Grimnar says acquiring new classes is hard and he has no more than three.
Klbkch explains that gaining levels gets exponentially harder over time.
Ryoka theorises that the system counts cumulative levels across all classes when working out how hard the next level is, so extra classes stunt a person's growth.
Klbkch is sceptical that cumulative levels matter or that a maximum level of one hundred exists, as that needs unproven suppositions.
Klbkch says the first Grand Queen reached Level 79 as a [Supreme Matriarch], a special class gained by advancing as a [Queen] for centuries, and had only one other class.
Klbkch reviews his Hive's data on several hundred high-level individuals and finds their cumulative levels rarely approach one hundred and that those with more than two classes rarely pass Level 30.
Selys, hearing the theory, worries that her many classes mean she will never reach a high level.
Flos tells Trey and Teres in secret that the more classes one has, the weaker one becomes over time, and a person with one class will always reach a higher level than one with many.
Flos says this is a secret of rulers, which is why they forbid their offspring from taking up common classes.
Flos has kept the twins from taking classes such as [Servant] or [Warrior] without knowing what they will become.
Krshia fears that a single-class rule would force Gnoll cubs to choose roles very young, which she finds troubling.
Gnoll tribes are practical, and one day someone is a hunter and the next a cook, so specialisation would change tribal life.
Flos fears that if being a student counts as a class, schools like those of Earth would be dangerous, and says he must not allow them.
Klbkch says two classes may merge in some rare cases to create a new hybrid class, for example [Warrior] and [Strategist] into [Commander].
Klbkch speculates his [Swordslayer] and [Commander] have not merged because [Swordslayer] advances [Warrior], or because he may have wished to keep a pure combat class.
Klbkch had regarded class merging as a somewhat negative phenomenon until that day.

Olesm says that if you gain enough warrior levels it is possible to transition into a commander class, and the narration from Klbkch's viewpoint says enough levels in [Warrior] and [Strategist] would merge into a new class, usually [Commander], that some people could level in [Commander] right away, and that as far as Klbkch could tell merging was simply a way to consolidate levels.
Laken calls a sudden swap of classes "class consolidation" when Prost loses all his [Farmer] and [Builder] levels and one [Trader] level and gains Level 8 [Steward].
Laken thinks Prost's farming experience does not transfer into [Steward], which is a sacrifice, though he may keep some or all of his Skills.
Prost's new Skills include [Talent Finder] and [Eye of Need], which help him find the people best suited to a task.
Durene says a [Commander] could take the [Soldier] and [Sergeant] classes and turn them into one thing.

Rags's night of [Tactician] Level 16 and [Leader] to [Chieftain] Level 15 also announces "Class Consolidation: Scavenger removed" and "Class Consolidation: Tinkerer removed", and she gains the Skills [Tribe: Fleet Foot] and [Lesser Tinkering].
In a vision, the Goblin King's [Healer] class merged into his [Chieftain] class.
Pyrite's [Mining Chieftain] class was consolidated into [Magestone Chieftain], letting him use magic via gemstones without being a [Mage].
Rufelt assumes a consolidated class means Erin is at least Level 20.
Lyonette's [Beast Tamer] class is consolidated into [Worldly Princess].
When Lyonette's [Princess] class is restored, five classes ([Warrior], [Barmaid], [Beast Tamer], [Tactician], [Carer]) are removed as consolidated into [Worldly Princess] at Level 11.
Lyonette's [Worldly Princess] at Level 19 is described as a rare class consolidation before Level 20.
Pebblesnatch reaches [Cook] Level 10 and consolidates [Grabber] into [Forager Cook], gaining [Natural Oils] and [One More Portion].
The narrator calls [Forager Cook] not the best consolidation, still below [Chef], but notes it came at Level 10.
Goblin low-level classes like [Stirrer] and [Roaster] rarely consolidate into better ones.
Paige announces that she changed her class after levelling and calls it a class consolidation.
Politician-turned-minister Lyfelt gained [Politician] and consolidated it to [Minister].
Embria says no class consolidation combines [Sergeant] and [Spearmaster], so her father stays a [Spearmaster] and [Sergeant].
Gazi says her [War Scout] class is a product of her [Infiltrator], [Fighter], [Rider] and [Archer] classes over time, reached at Level 30.
Raelt, King of Jecrass, reaches Level 30 as [King] and the class becomes [King of Challenges], with [Duelist] consolidated away.
A [Hammerer] says he has consolidated twice.
Garia, a [Runner] training as a [Martial Artist], hopes to consolidate the two classes because both are about the body, though she has no idea what class she would get.
Lyonette's [Princess] class is lost when the system reports "Class Conditions: Princess failed", and she also loses [Detect Poison] and [Royal Tax].
Later "Class Conditions: Princess met" restores the class and the lost skills, and the class turns into [Worldly Princess].
Lyonette wonders if she lost her [Princess] class because she had no subjects or kingdom, or had given it up.
Klbkch says each time the Queen resurrects him, he loses ten levels from his classes, an occurrence found only among the Antinium.
Klbkch is currently Level 21 [Swordslayer], Level 18 [Commander], Level 11 [Diplomat] and Level 14 [Assassin], but at his peak he was Level 44 [Swordslayer] and Level 26 [Assassin].

Klbkch says the Rite of Anastases is a process the Queen of the Antinium may undertake to let the dead be reborn into a new body, that only a Prognugator would be considered worthy of the effort, that he lost ten levels in every class, and that his Queen laboured nearly three weeks without rest.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Val describes skills as a safe gamble: each level gives some good and some less useful skills, but which ones you may get can be predicted from the class, like a pool of options.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Val says almost every close-range [Warrior] gets [Thick Skin] sooner or later, but one might get it at Level 5 and another much later.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Val agrees with Ryoka's guess that there are rare skills every ten levels, and says a rare skill can also be learned, but that takes training and some luck.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Klbkch says there is no one set of skills for a class; skills depend on need and inclination.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Pisces says classes and Skills are acquired often in line with the user's desires, and he has no Skills for summoning flesh-based undead.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Garia got [Lesser Strength] on her second level up as a [Farm Worker]; she says it is the first skill most warriors get, followed by the stronger [Enhanced Strength] and, for very high levels, [Greater Strength].

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Selys says no one in Liscor has [Expert Cooking], that you would have to be a really high-level [Chef] to have it, and that it might appear at Level 40, or maybe Level 30 if you got lucky.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Erin gains [Advanced Cooking] and [Advanced Crafting] on reaching Level 21 as an [Innkeeper], while [Basic Cooking] came at Level 1.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Erin complains that finding a [Cook] with [Advanced Cooking] is hard because people with that Skill are rare.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Ryoka concludes that skills can be rated by rarity, which generally corresponds to level.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Klbkch tells Pisces that [Detect Guilt] is a basic skill all guardsmen learn at Level 15.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Skill usage can be limited: Olesm says he can use one Skill only once a day at his level and that his other skills are mostly defensive or informational.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Laken's Skills show that some are permanent passive changes, such as Durene's [Enhanced Strength], while others must be used.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Lyonette recalls a tutor saying a Skill improves what is already there, so [Basic Cooking] without actual cooking experience gives only basic results.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Some Skills can be copied by learning the technique: Klbkch says [Triple Thrust], three literally simultaneous strikes, cannot be copied by mere technique, but others are crystallised forms that can be taught.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Jasi's Skill summons exactly five gold pieces' worth of supplies before a performance; she hopes it upgrades, as some Skills do, and tells Rima to wait until Level 20.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Skill names can carry a prefix for what they affect, such as [Tribe: Fleet Foot], [Inn: Magical Grounds] and [Army: Flicker Charge].

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Erin's [Magical Innkeeper] skills [Inn: Magical Grounds] and [Inn: Field of Preservation] arrive at Level 30.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Erin imagines a Level 40 message granting [Inn: Unlimited Mana Pool] and [Kamehameha Punch] and waits for the real voice, but nothing comes.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Pisces's Level 30 Skill gave him greater mastery of bone shaping, though Draugr creation was a common alternative at that level.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Skills that work on others can be resisted: Pisces says any powerful monster or individual will resist most of an aura Skill, though it works well on low-level enemies.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Lyonette teaches that auras have potency, which is their power, and control, which is how they are used; she tells Erin she has high potency but her control is weak.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Lyonette says she consolidated her aura into something that works like a shield, while Erin's aura is too wide and works like a hammer.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Val says that other Runners will only become Couriers if they get really lucky and learn a good skill.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Skills are not always known to their owners: Erin cannot recall what her new [Inn's Aura] and [Wondrous Fare] skills do right after waking.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: A ruler's Skill can apply to the whole kingdom, such as Flos's Skill that makes his soldiers level up quicker, and such kingdom-wide Skills are rare even for rulers.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Flos says a [King] can issue conditional Skills like edicts, but only one edict is active, and a new one replaces the first.

section: Skills: how they are gained and what they do
text: Flos says Mars's Skills are almost all specific to herself, while his affect more people.
A silver-bearded mage says his appraisal and identification spells could not read Ryoka's class or level, though she is neither undead nor construct and entirely human.
Cervial can use an [Appraisal] skill that [Marksmen] sometimes get, and says he cannot see Ryoka's Level or Class.
A bald mage says he does not know that Ryoka is levelless, but another adventurer with [Appraisal] says it is true.
Saliss tells Erin he can see a few basic facts about her but not her Skills, and that he keeps people's levels secret.
Later the narration states that Saliss's Skill [Eyes of Appraisal] shows him Erin's level, class and Skills.
Saliss has already known one of Erin's Skills before it is revealed, which Erin resolves to remember.
Ceria is amazed that Ksmvr is only Level 16, having assumed from how he fights that he was at least Level 20.

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: Class changes use lines such as "[Conditions Met: Warrior → General Class!]".

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: Consolidations list each removed class, for example "[Class Consolidation: Warrior removed.]".

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: A [Condition] line can follow a level message: the Earther [Clown] receives "[Condition – Horrific Laughter Received.]" and "[Condition – Lesser Insanity Received.]" when she reaches Level 24.

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: The [Condition] lines can be removed: the Florist turned monster later gets "[Condition – Terrible Hunger Removed!]".

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: A monster-making change uses its own format: "[Rank 1 Horror – Corpse Eater.]" with Conditions "Terrible Hunger" and "Outcast Humanity", and [Aspect] lines like "Body of the Eater".

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: When the Florist became a Horror, her [Florist] level dropped from 19 to 16 and she lost [Aroma of Spring] and [Winter Growth]; at Rank 2 she dropped to 12 and lost [Quick Growth] and gained [Gaping Bite].

section: Conditions, aspects and other system messages
text: Skills lost or restored are announced the same way, as with Lyonette's [Detect Poison] and [Royal Tax].
Ceria says mages level from casting spells, but study also gives a lot of experience, so throwing fireballs alone does not level fast.
Val says [Warriors] level faster by killing stronger enemies, while [Runners] level by how far they run and how challenging the run is.
Calruz is called a Levelist because he fights any enemy just to gain experience.
Garen tells Rags training only works when it hurts, and Rags learns that levelling by training is possible but slow, which she finds common knowledge among non-Goblins.

Belgrade says chess is important because it teaches strategic thinking and asks why so many [Tacticians] and [Strategists] play it; a reply says it makes one level, and Anand says he could understand a low-level [Tactician] benefiting but finds more than five or six levels suspect for a high-level [Strategist].
The Counter-level Effect, according to Pisces, means defenders in a war level faster than superior aggressors, and Zel Shivertail was an example.
Desperate fighting in narrow corridors during the Antinium Wars led to "explosive leveling" among the defenders.
Erin objects that the Counter-level Effect only works if the defenders are losing.
After a day of frantic effort, Erin has gained four levels and two skills.
Lyonette, after not having been a [Princess] for a long time, levelled four times in one day and thinks it may be because [Barmaid] reached Level 15.
A Dragon tells Erin he has met legends who reached higher levels than hers at her age, but never an [Innkeeper] who rose as she did.

section: Refusing to level and levelless people
text: Ryoka stopped herself from levelling, saying she does not like being controlled and thinks classes and levels are a way for a system to control people.

section: Refusing to level and levelless people
text: Ryoka says she can cancel a level-up if she thinks hard enough.

section: Refusing to level and levelless people
text: Adventurers who learn Ryoka has no levels ask whether she is a demi-human, a monster, or a fool.

section: Refusing to level and levelless people
text: Val says that he meets people who choose not to level now and then, and that they overcome the problem with magic.

section: Refusing to level and levelless people
text: Ryoka tells Selys and Klbkch that one can refuse to level up or take a class, and Selys says she never understood why that was possible.

section: Refusing to level and levelless people
text: Ryoka suspects that choice exists precisely because of the level-cap problem.
Ryoka learns that a Bronze-rank adventuring team is not much better than rookies, while a Silver-rank team is more than a match for a small city's standing militia.
Gold-rank adventurers are experienced, highly trained groups that handle most monster threats easily, and at the top of the rank teams equal small armies and can affect disputes between nations.
Gold is as high as most ranking systems go; some countries extend ranks into platinum and adamantium, but functionally a party or individual at that renown is no longer ranked.
Past Gold-rank, adventurers are called Named Adventurers because their names are known across the part of the world where they travel.
Cervial adds that individual skill still plays a big role, and Yvlon says Calruz is only around Level 20 but could have joined a Gold-rank team.
A confirmed old magical dungeon is expected to pull in Named Adventurers and Gold-rank adventurers, possibly from other continents.
Ryoka understands that Yvlon and Cervial rely on magical equipment along with levels, while Calruz the Levelist thinks levels are all he needs.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Antinium Workers have very few levels; Pawn is a Level 2 [Butcher] and Level 1 [Carpenter], and some Workers do not level at all.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Selys thinks Antinium Soldiers do not need levels and would be an unstoppable army if they were given high levels and produced in numbers.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Erin says Pawn told her other Workers have levelled in [Tactician], probably the Goblins too, though she has none.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: A Drake guard tells Erin that Klbkch was the only Antinium he had heard of with a level higher than 10.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Ryoka states that the Queen's mission is to create Individual Antinium capable of levelling, which would make the Antinium stronger, and Klbkch nods.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: The new Antinium Individuals level far quicker than Klbkch or the Queen.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Ksmvr says the Antinium do not level except Individuals, and that he was Level 12 when he met Ceria and is now a Level 16 [Warrior].

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Ksmvr says Antinium do not level greatly, so magic was not seen as a viable field for them.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Klbkch reflects that Individuals can level exponentially quickly by Antinium standards and are closer to Prognugators, but true Hive Soldiers are stronger to begin with.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Klbkch holds the class [Diplomat] at Level 11 and uses its Level 10 Skill [Reassuring Presence] daily; no one, not even his Queen, knows he has these tertiary classes, which he understands inhibit his levelling.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Garen, whose tribe is the Red Fang Tribe, has no levels in [Chieftain] or [Leader], and his idea of leadership is leading a small group of warriors into combat.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: A Hobgoblin [Stirrer] is described as a low-level cook not yet at the [Cook] class, which happens when a Goblin gets to Level 10.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Erin's lessons gave some Cave Goblins the [Cook] class straight away, without waiting for Level 10.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: A Selphid can have levels like anyone else: Calectus is a Level 36 [Honor Guard], the senior and highest-level of the Selphids with Geneva.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: A character says any undead that can level will eventually rebel, like Golems, and Pisces replies that Toren proved it possible, though Toren levelled quickly enough to subvert his control.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Toren sees that common skeletons cannot restore themselves and have no levels, unlike him.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Fetohep says that as a Revenant, one of the few undead who keep their will, he does not level but keeps all the Skills he had in life.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Fierre says Vampires do not earn classes or level up, and her mother lost her classes when she became a vampire.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Fierre says Old Bamer thinks the lack of Vampire levels is a way of keeping balance, and asks the listener to imagine a high-level [Warrior] who was a vampire.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Fierre says Old Bamer told her Vampire Lords of old had Skills and could turn to mist, though she thinks that may be a relic of the past.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Fierre reflects that a Vampire gains no levels, like an animal or sub-races such as Ogres or the true Giants of old, while even Goblins level.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Erin tells a group of adventurers that Raskghar are big and strong but cannot level.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: An adventurer says the Raskghar do not have Skills and so can be prepared for.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Krshia imagines Raskghar as primal Gnolls who cannot level but are stronger than modern Gnolls, based on legends too old to give specifics.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: A Grand Strategist says regular Raskghar are around a Level 15 Gnoll [Warrior] unless it is a full moon, when with increased abilities they are Level 20 at best, and that awakened Raskghar are different.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: A council member in the same scene says Raskghar without Skills are inherently weaker and will not level, but can go into fighting without needing to level.

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: The Gnoll council in the city chooses the oldest, wisest, most experienced or highest-level Gnolls in place of a [Chieftain].

section: Levels in non-humans and other beings
text: Krshia's authority among them comes partly from a relatively high level.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: A [Runner] belongs to roughly three kinds: Street Runners within one city, City Runners across a region, and Couriers who go anywhere and are each at least Level 30 per Garia, with levels in other classes.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Fals says few experienced Runners exist because no one lives long doing the job, and most change class after earning enough.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: A [Healer] uses herbs and minor spells, while a [Cleric] or high-level mage-healer is needed for serious wounds and such healers are very rare.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: A [Healer] who says he is not high-level tells Yvlon that perhaps one with a Skill, or a [Bone Surgeon] from a Gnoll tribe's rare healers, might deal with her affliction, but that as it is he can do nothing.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: The best [Healer] in Bolandus, who reached out to Geneva, is Level 37, and Geneva lectures a sixty-year-old Dullahan [Healer] over Level 30 about her treatment.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Pisces says wizard, sorcerer, warlock and witch are titles for mages who meet certain requirements, and mage is the general term.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Pisces says the spell that shortens the storm could easily be cast by a Level 30 mage, or by a lower-level one if specialised.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Pisces lists his levels as fifteen in [Elementalist], eight in [Alchemist], six in [Enchanter] and ten in [Mage], and says a single level in the [Necromancer] class makes a mage killed on sight in this region.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Yvlon's longsword was made by a Level 32 [Blacksmith], and Flos asks a merchant for masterworks made by a Level 40 [Blacksmith] or better.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Olesm's class [Tactician] is the first step of the strategist class line, and Pisces says it is useless in small groups unless the holder has combat skill.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Niers Astoragon is called the highest-leveled [Strategist] on the continent, yet in the same chapter he is a Level 63 [Tactician].

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Anand tells Belgrade that understanding war beyond games is key to being a [Strategist] and not simply a [Tactician], and says Belgrade will reach the class first.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Yvlon is a [Warrior] who in her own eyes does not deserve the [Knight] class, though her armament is a [Knight]'s.

section: Common class families, as the text shows them
text: Saliss says the owner of the Noble's Fancy in Pallass is over Level 30 and an inn near First Landing is run by a Level 50 plus [Innkeeper].

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Ryoka reasons that Olesm and the others level from chess and Erin does not because there is no [Gamer] class, suggesting the system's designer or the culture had not yet adapted to casual play, and tables the idea as unconfirmed.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: A faerie tells Ryoka that having put the chains on willingly, her classes and levels make her a plaything, and that she does not know who plays this game.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Ryoka thinks levels and classes are a way for the world or some system to control people.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Klbkch asks Ryoka and Selys to keep the cumulative-level theory quiet until it is certain.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Ryoka believes most people never hit a level cap, and the few who do mistake it for old age.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Flos treats the rule that more classes mean a lower reachable level as a secret of rulers who reach high levels.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Pisces says that classes are based on what we pursue and trivial things fail to trigger them in some people.

section: Misreadings, theories and secrets about the system
text: Anand says that a high-level [Strategist] levelling from a game like chess would make him almost suspect an error in the way we level, and another speaker replies that this would mean an error in the world.
Pisces says magic has seven or eight tiers, with a speculative ninth tier that no mage has cast or discovered.
Pisces says he cannot cast beyond the third tier in any field and is mostly limited to first and second tier within his specialisations.
A book Ryoka read says a spell a mage below Level 16 can cast is generally 1st or 0 Tier, up to about Level 24 is 2nd Tier, and up to Level 32 is 3rd Tier.
The same book says lower-level mages can cast higher-Tier magic with enough practice and time.
Ceria says magic comes in Tiers, and that she would call [Light] Tier 0 if she could, since it is one of the most basic magics people learn.
Ceria names [Spark] as another example of a very basic spell, like making light or making heat.
Ryoka calls [Noise] a Tier 0 spell that Ceria taught her.
Ceria puts [Ice Spike] and [Detect Magic] at Tier 3, [Ice Shard] at Tier 2 and [Frozen Wind] at Tier 1.
Ceria says Tier 3 magic is good for fighting so long as the target is not too deadly.
Ceria is unsure whether [Haste] is Tier 4 or Tier 5.
Ceria says she can cast Tier 3 magic at best, and that a Tier 4 spell would need a spellbook and weeks or months at her level.
Ceria says that learning a spell such as [Grand Fireball] would take her years even if she knew how it was supposed to go.
Pisces knows one Tier 4 spell, [Invisibility], which nearly killed him to learn and cost him a month of studying every night for at least two hours.
Pisces learned [Invisibility] at Level 18 and gained two levels from learning it.
Ceria sees Illphres cast a Tier 4 spell, [Ice Lance], in seconds without a wand.
Rievan taught the whole class [Electric Jolt], and Pisces, who knew no Tier 2 combat spells, practised it too.
Pisces says he finds Tier 1 spells unchallenging to make work optimally, like a map with the destination circled.
Ceria and Pisces disagree about [Stone Fist]: she says it is a good Tier 3 spell and he thought it Tier 2.
Ceria's early spells [Stone Dart], [Flame Jet] and [Chameleon] are described as barely Tier 2.
An old man fighting the Horns of Hammerad calls [Stone Dart] a low level spell but all he is capable of there, and says only Tier 2 spells will be necessary.
Calvaron says there are plenty of mages in Wistram who can cast Tier 5 or even Tier 6 spells, and higher than that is out of reach without getting past Cognita.
Ceria tells Ryoka that half-elves of old all learned Tier 2 magic before their teens, according to her grandfather.

Ceria says items have an intensity like magic's tiers and rates the items she and Pisces study, a sword and rings among them, as Tier 1, perhaps Tier 2 on one ring at best, adding that Tier 1 is still good.
Ceria, analysing a powerful trap spell of blue flames set off by digging into a secret corridor, wonders whether it is Tier 5 or 6.
Ceria says wands amplify your magic, hold stored energy that may or may not restore over time, and some contain spells that can be triggered once or several times.
Ceria says artifacts are like wands but usually with recharging mana and deeper reserves, and warns never to tell anyone you own one because some people will kill for it.
Ceria says [Ice Spike] is a matter of shaping the energy and that she could cast it once without a wand, but the backlash would hurt.
Adding more mana to a [Light] orb can make it bigger or differently shaped, and Ryoka makes hers brighter by adding energy; Ceria calls such variations exercises that help control.
Ceria says only a really good mage can control a thrown [Light] orb at a distance.
Ceria says mages cannot form spells from nothing: the images in their heads become the spells, so she cannot make light as bright as the sun.
Ceria says most mages have specialties, something they understand; she understands cold because she spent winters in snow and ice.
Ryoka recalls learning [Light] as closer to a mathematical revelation or solving a formula, and later thinks of controlling the power as pushing or pulling, or absorbing and releasing.

In Wistram, basic telekinesis, magical composition and spellcraft are lumped into one category called elementary or 'pure' magic, which matters for any mage who wants to cast spells because badly formed spells are less effective.
A Wistram teacher criticises spells that are leaking pools of wasted mana and wants well-formed ones.
The narrator notes that the more complex a spell is, the more a mage benefits from working with it, after Rievan insists that students who know a higher-Tier spell practise that instead.
A Wistram teacher praises Pisces for diverting the whole of his electrical spell into his other palm without letting the individual threads of magic separate as the electricity desires.
The image of the target in the caster's mind is as important as the pointing finger for the angle and trajectory a thrown spell takes.
Wind can blow a spell off course, and past fifty feet Ceria's aim worsens.
Pisces warns that magic, unlike a hammer or sewing needle, can slay an incautious practitioner outright even when the spell seems mastered.
Ceria feels as if she is burning away her very soul when she reaches her limit, and her wand-hand burns with the backlash of a spell.
Repeatedly casting even low-Tier spells is extremely draining.
Ceria says leveling in the [Mage] class is a great way to learn a new spell and much faster than teaching yourself, though a person can learn magic without a class.
Ceria says magic requires study even with levels.
Ceria says putting enough time and effort into a spell lets you master it, but there are limits.
Ceria says that if she gained ten levels overnight learning a hard spell would be far easier, though understanding how it works would do as well.
Ceria says that with a spellbook she can study a spell and learn it in a year or so.
Ceria says a single spellbook costs several hundred gold or even a thousand, even for low-Tier spells.
Ceria says she would need a few hundred gold more to buy a book with a few Tier 4 spells.
Ceria says neither she nor Pisces can cast [Fireball], and that she used a wand when she had to cast it.
Ryoka learned [Light] from Ceria in a single day.
Pisces says he benefited from someone showing him how to cast [Electric Jolt] and found the way the teacher optimised it quite interesting.
Calvaron says Wistram hands new students old spellbooks left behind by students, and the older mages sort them so nothing beyond a Tier 2 spell goes to newcomers.
Spellbooks given to new Wistram students are mostly empty apprentice books with the first pages filled with another person's notes and spells.
Ceria has heard that spellbooks are warded against being read, and Pisces says the book they are after apparently killed the student who tried to take it out.
Pisces uses [Detect Magic] to spot the most powerful spellbooks among a shelf of books.
After days of decoding a spell from the library spellbook, Pisces suddenly blurs and appears several feet forward in an instant.
Calvaron says that older students need masters because it is too hard to progress otherwise, given the limited number of spellbooks.

Calvaron says many mages do not want to teach younger mages, so students persuade them with services, such as him getting his master almost anything he needs or Beatrice helping her master with his spells.
A mage may have several apprentices and teach all of them, or just one.
Ceria says half-elves are gifted at magic, with more of it in their bodies, but do not learn spells any faster.
Ceria thinks half-elves channel mana better than any other species.
The isle of Wistram opens only one day a year to accept new students.
Ceria is told to present herself at the docks in South Harbor, Belan, Terandria, and boards a ship there for the isle of Wistram.
Attending Wistram Academy costs twenty gold pieces for a month.
Anyone with magic who can pay the fee can enter Wistram, and applicants prove their ability to an examiner by showing spells.
The captain of the Errant Traveller tells boarding students to cause no trouble and cast no magic on his ship, and Ceria recalls the others being told the same.
The ship's captain checks arrivals against a paper list that shows each student's face in turn, which Ceria recognises as magic.
Prospective students have just over a month to prove themselves and be accepted or sent home.
Wistram trains Mages mainly but also students heading to related fields such as [Alchemist] or [Blacksmith], so long as magic is involved.
New students take mandatory basic courses in their first month from mid-level [Mages].
New students get ink pots, quills and a low-level spellbook on their first day.
Calvaron says the Wistram classes teach only the basics because most magic-based classes need at least ten levels in [Mage], and many take at least twenty.
Wistram law states that mages below the third year are allowed only one personal spellbook.
Many new students wear long robes, usually dark blue or black, bought with a low-quality wand; older students such as Calvaron and Beatrice do not.
Ceria sees a wall end a few feet ahead of a pair of doors beside a diagonal junction of three corridors, and feels that architecture and the laws of space do not seem to matter in Wistram.

A general central area of Wistram holds dormitories, classrooms and general storage, while the higher levels and lower recesses are off-limits to new students, with magical barriers, locked doors or Golems at stairwells.
Wistram has many libraries; some hold one subject, one era, or a pool where books are waterproofed for bathing readers.
Mages in the windowless parts of the citadel can wander for hours without seeing the sun.
Wistram's students include Humans, Drakes, a Selphid, a Centaur and Dullahans.
Dullahans commonly study rune magic, and Beatrice, a Dullahan, is a [Runeshaper] whose armor is etched with runes.
Golems clear dishes in Wistram unless students levitate them to another table.
Mages at Wistram eat well, and students share a grand dining hall.
Outside her door Ceria uses [Detect Magic] and finds a hex on the flagstones that would make the ground slippery like grease and a second, hidden trap spell, which she takes to be a shock spell.
Ceria thinks Wistram has few totally absolute rules, and Pisces suspects some restrictions are warnings meant to test how students react.
Wistram students trade secrets as a currency, such as unique classes or where treasure is buried, for coin or other secrets.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: The entrance exam at the end of the first month tests students on fundamental magic control, analysing enchantments, composure in battle and a final obstacle course allowing attack spells.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Entrance exam rankings feed bets and power games, and wealth or the favour of influential mages can also decide who passes.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Of the hundreds who come each year, less than a tenth pass the entrance exams.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Failed students are picked up by chartered ships the day after the yearly exams.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Students from the second year onward face yearly qualification tests, which Ceria describes as proving you have learned something, such as a spell, a recitation or something made.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: A mage who fails to show progress may be forced to pay to stay, from a little for food and lodging to a lot.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Pisces tells Montressa that second-year students are not tested nearly as harshly as older students such as Calvaron and Beatrice.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Duels are fairly common among Wistram students, with a shield spell protecting onlookers, and students duel for money, pride or anything else.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Wistram also has spoken debates, decided by collective vote; voters must answer under a truth spell about who made the more convincing argument.

section: Wistram Academy: exams, tests and duels
text: Calvaron says the Council eases new students into life and does not allow fights on the first day.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Wistram has been around for thousands of years, founded when many nations were at war and mages wanted somewhere to learn and teach in peace.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Wistram has always been independent: no nation controls it, it has an army of its own, and a fleet reaching its shores would face raised weather spells.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Cessic says, on a tip he bought cheaply from Calvaron, that the Council, made up of the leaders of all the mage factions, chewed out the mage in charge of a class and told them to start teaching right away.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The class [Archmage] exists, and the [Archmages] who ruled Wistram a few centuries ago all held it.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Archmage Zelkyr was a Drake and the best of the [Archmages], famous for damaging a Walled City wall and for creating Golems.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Zelkyr, with Cognita and an army of Golems, took undisputed control of Wistram and alone explored its higher reaches for ancient magics.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The greatest mages in Wistram's history settled the highest floors, leaving creations, spells and rooms that are deadly traps to break into.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: After Cognita announced that Zelkyr was dead, she and the other Golems maintain Wistram, fight intruders and enforce his order that no one may venture above.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Calvaron says that today the Archmages of Wistram are only the greatest mages there, not holders of the class, and that factions formed because no mage can control everyone.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Factions are groups of mages with similar ideals who stick together when it comes to voting or pushing their agendas.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Calvaron advises new students not to join a faction before passing the exam.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Calvaron stays independent, and factions keep each other in check so independents can function.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Calvaron says only the Expansionists and Revivalists care about making sure there is a system for new students, though every faction usually contributes somehow.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The Revivalists are one faction; Beatrice calls it hers and invites Ceria and Pisces to join if they pass the exam.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The Isolationists want only mages already strong admitted and reaching for greater heights; Illphres belongs to them.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The Libertarians want Wistram to take sides with nations and throw its influence around; many are from Terandria, and Rievan belongs to them.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The Centrists want every mage in the world to be part of Wistram, and for Wistram to declare itself a nation.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: The Preservationists and Revivalists would protect Ceria from an Elementalist teacher, to avoid a rumour that Wistram is speciesist.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Teaching posts are filled by mages who like it or earn their keep by it; when the old Drake Tshya died, the Preservationists insisted on teachers from all factions, which got Rievan the job, and the Centrists nominated Illphres.

section: Wistram Academy: history, Archmages and factions
text: Pisces reports that the Libertarians want every new student they can get and tried to recruit him before the exam.
Ceria feels magic flow into her hand when she readies a spell.
A mana potion Ceria has taken helps her recover after a fight, and in another scene she throws up a bit as one runs through her system.
A mage whose face is grey has used too much magic, and Ceria's mana potion helps her recover from the same strain.
Ceria says she could cast [Illumination] only once before needing a mana potion, since casting it repeatedly is too exhausting.
Halrac recognises paleness as the first symptom of mana exhaustion, and a [Mage] who is exhausted may vomit.

Gerial says that without mana a mage team can do little, so Lir's team will often abandon a mission if something makes them use up all their potions or the enemy proves more numerous or stronger than expected.
Pisces is still pale from mana exhaustion after a hard fight.
Pisces is out of mana and Ceria is nearly tapped after a dungeon fight.
Rievan teaches that mana may over-accumulate in a body from a spell or from a charged environment, but more often from improperly drinking a mana potion.
Rievan teaches that casting any spell usually resolves excess mana in a mage, while those without mana can only rest.
Rievan teaches that a competent mage may drain excess magic from another, which carries risk, and that high concentrations can rupture blood vessels or shut down body parts.
The occupant of the cave, tending the unconscious Ryoka, notes she is suffering from mana poisoning, which is far more difficult to cure than mere blood loss.
Teriarch says the mana Ryoka drank would not have killed her; he says she would have had violent illness, fever and uncontrollable bodily excretion for days.
Teriarch says a minuscule increase in diet is the only proper way to acclimatise a human body to magic, and he doubts modern mages know how to naturalise magic within themselves.
Mana potions and alcohol do not mix well, according to a mage.
Ryoka's mana-poisoned state followed her drinking mana potions she thought were healing potions; Ceria had given them to her by mistake.
Octavia is trying to standardise potion colours so adventurers do not use a mana potion instead of a healing potion.
Erin wonders whether mana potions could make food magical.
Everything contains magic: Octavia says traces are in rocks and grass, and something like a mana stone has quite a lot.
Fals says he hears that the powerful magic coaches, which create horses out of magic, have to replace mana stones or recharge the magic quite often.
A construct in a dungeon keeps a glowing mana stone in its chest.
Healing potions cost a gold coin or two, rising with potency, according to Ryoka's early market survey.
A weak healing potion costs nearly a gold coin.
