The City Watch in Liscor carries healing potions, and Senior Guardsmen carry stronger ones that fix most big injuries unless a limb is lost.
Klbkch gives Erin part of what he calls a low-grade healing potion, which closes a cut on her hand in an instant.
Healing potions only accelerate the body's natural healing; Ceria says complicated injuries such as a shattered bone need time or magic.
A mage says that healing potions can fuse bone back together wrongly, leaving fighters with bones attached off-center.
A stronger healing potion would start growing bone fragments out of the skin and destroy the leg, Ryoka is told.
Geneva observes a cheap healing potion closing existing tissue at an accelerated rate rather than creating new skin.
Geneva infers cheap potions would not manage bad breaks, cannot heal severed limbs and can inhibit reattachment if used wrongly.
Thriss says the better type of healing potion removes poison and other problems, while his cheap potions do not.
Geneva explains that potions do not cure disease, they accelerate natural functions, so they can make a disease worse and kill everyone it infects.
Geneva says plagues are far more deadly in this world because of potions.
Stamina potions restore energy and give a kick, but they do not heal a torn muscle and the user crashes hard when they wear off.
Ryoka finds Octavia's stamina potion tastes awful, and Octavia prices them at a gold piece and eight silver each.
Ryoka runs for a night and a day on one of Octavia's stamina potions and Octavia warns it can only stave off exhaustion for so long.
Ryoka falls asleep once a stamina potion wears off and resolves never to overuse one again.
Octavia says she could not brew invisibility potions, and that a regeneration potion would need fifty more levels.
Octavia identifies Teriarch's potion as a potion of haste or a higher-level version, made with top ingredients and perfectly heated.
Teriarch pays Ryoka for a delivery with a Potion of Haste that shifts colours when removed from its stand.
Octavia says potions can be any colour and she is trying to standardise them, and she offers a yellow potion for a wound.
Octavia says she is no mage and that alchemy needs only magical ingredients are rendered down by boiling and mixing and then combined.
Octavia says everything has some magic, and an extracted magical quality can be stored in a base liquid so more ingredients can be added.
Octavia says alchemy depends on order, heat and time: moon dew can be used only at night under a waxing moon, and Goblin ears must be boiled while mixing.
Octavia says alchemy is unpredictable and dangerous, and covers more than potions, such as a tripvine bag.
Octavia's custom-order price for testing and delivery of Ryoka's potions is eight gold, and she is not sure everything asked is possible.
An [Alchemist] sifts saltpeter, sulfur, charcoal and wood dust together with a material that catches fire in open air for Ryoka.

Teriarch, watching an image of Octavia and Erin, calls the white potion Octavia tosses into a smoking pot a neutralizing potion and says the carrots should have been mixed with a cold agent before the Corusdeer horns.
Eir Gel from a single island off Baleros is the foundation for modern healing potions and supplies nearly the whole world.
Octavia says every [Alchemist] has their own recipe, and potions differ because one missing or extra ingredient changes the result.
Octavia's cheap booster is made from Sage's Grass, sugar water, powdered demi-Newt skins and roach shells.
Octavia says Sage's Grass was bred by a powerful [Sage] and was once the most powerful ingredient in the world.
Octavia says alchemy survives where mage empires collapse because dead alchemists leave notes and ingredients, which is why cheap potions can close a big wound today.
Octavia says Skills decide which potions an [Alchemist] can make; her basic healing potion uses [Low-Grade Synthesis], [Cleansing Heat], [Mineral Distillation] and [Magic-Water Solvent].
Octavia notes a wide base on glassware lets more heat reach the mixture.
Pisces says he knows of only a few living mages who might attempt a long-range teleportation like the one that brought Erin to the world.
Teriarch says teleportation spells are not easy even for him.
Someone pursuing Magnolia's party reasons that with no spell circle and no one able to teleport long distances so quickly, the fast movement must be to a prearranged destination.
Teriarch touches a teleportation circle on the floor, and its symbols glow bright, to send Ryoka away.
Gazi opens a portal about eight feet by eight feet wide, ringed by spinning symbols, that stretches her foot thousands of miles to a patch of grass ringed by runestones.
The tunnel of light closes after Gazi steps through, and a spear thrown through it lands back in the grass on Erin's side.
A teleportation scroll is an item Ryoka sees Gazi carrying.
A Wistram student thinks a monster in the dining hall might come from a teleportation spell gone wrong.
A ring of [Lesser Teleportation] is fixed to an anchor that no mage can discern, and putting it on might be deadly.
A [Teleportation] spell can cost a buyer dearly.
Adventurers swap a rumour of a mage who teleported the people in a trap into a pit in the middle of bedrock with no way out, and elsewhere someone cries that a trap teleported them.
Pisces explains that the dungeon door cannot be destroyed and has a potent teleportation spell worked into it.
Pisces says the door is only half of the spell and a small object, usually a stone, acts as the anchor for the teleportation.
Pisces says the door and its anchor stone can be used to teleport to the stone, or the reverse, any number of times.
Pisces says the door's magic replenishes by absorbing natural mana in the environment, though each activation needs a huge amount.
Pisces says a normal [Teleportation] spell can carry someone a long way, and Gazi's customised long-distance spell took her across an ocean.
Pisces estimates the door could manage one or two mass teleportations a day unless a way to recover mana is found.
Pisces and Moore, speaking for the mages, say the door can send someone of Ryoka's general weight, give or take twenty pounds, 536 miles and would then need roughly 8.2 hours to recharge fully.
Erin tells Ilvriss her door goes only as far as Invrisil, carries one person at a time, and takes a day to recharge.
Erin says she could recharge faster with mana stones, but that wouldn't make the door go further.
Erin needs an anchor placed at a destination before her door can connect to it, so a Courier must carry one there.
Hawk sets up the anchor in Pallass and opens a link between the inn door and the Walled City; the link carries one person at a time and then needs twenty-four hours.
Pallass guards declare Jelaqua, Relc and their party under arrest, saying they teleported in with an unauthorized spell and that they tracked their position.
Moore pries loose the coloured mana stone that Typhenous and Pisces attuned to the door, and the Pallass mages report the link between the doors broken.
Later, the inn's door switches between destinations by placing a corresponding coloured mana stone on it.
Scrying needs the exact name of the person to be seen, or failing that a piece of clothing or some part of them, according to Teriarch's reasoning.
Pisces says most mages use the [Farsight] and [Scrying] spells to gaze with impunity on anyone they like.
A mage who tried to scry Ryoka by the name he was given failed, and Ryoka guesses he would need her true Japanese name.
An Orb of Scrying embedded in pure jade and enchanted to increase its range and scope can show what is in the room around it.
Ilvriss talks to other Lords and Ladies of the Wall through paired scrying orbs, which are very expensive and leave the conversation open to eavesdroppers.
Real-time conferences by magic are difficult to organise, though Wistram can devise complex spells to allow them.
[Message] sends the equivalent of a short magical email, and Ryoka thinks the mana cost depends on distance and perhaps atmosphere.
Adventurers use [Message] to send requests to the local Mage's Guild, whose price rises sharply with urgency.
Pisces says that for a group discussion each recipient would need a [Message] spell, so the cost is multiplied by the number of participants.
Nesor is a poor [Mage] who cannot process [Message] spells like an experienced spellcaster, and Garusa says none of their [Mages] can cast [Message] despite daily attempts.
A [Message] spell incoming gives a telltale flickering of the recipient's eyes.
Zel Shivertail's and Ilvriss's [Message] spells reached the Drake cities almost instantly, while Human cities heard the next morning.
A [Message] can be marked with the highest priority reserved for emergencies under Drake protocols.
A speaking stone worn on a dress can carry Magnolia's voice.
A rare gem artifact communicates across the world, is limited in power, and disintegrates when out of mana.
Cognita describes herself as a Carved Golem, or rather a Truestone Construct, designed to oversee Wistram and its mages.
Cognita says that most Wistram Golems lack intelligence and simply obey orders, and warns students not to attack or obstruct them.
Cognita requires anyone casting area-wide magic in Wistram to consult her or an experienced mage first.
Truestone Golems were thought to be the pinnacle of artificial creation, and Cognita alone has personality, thought and feeling.
Pisces argues that Golems require high-grade materials such as mana stones and rock without impurity, being products of spellcraft and superior base material.
Teriarch tells Magnolia that a Gemstone Golem would have more utility, that Ivory Golems are too susceptible to interference via death magic, and suggests a Magestone or even a Truestone Golem.
In the dungeon the Goblins enter, two Stone Golems posing as statues kill Goblins, and fifteen Stone Golems pursue the survivors until they flee back through the hole.
Magnolia Reinhart's estate is guarded by silvery metal Golems gilded with pink metal that patrol the grounds with mechanical precision.
Snow Golems are bodies of snow bound by magic, and when the magic is dug out of the head the body slumps apart.
The snow in a Snow Golem's head is unnaturally pure and magical.
Natural Golems of stone can appear on their own, especially in areas with a lot of magicore, and they cause havoc.
Zelkyr's test: defeat his guardians, four Golems plus Cognita.
A Drake in Pallass says Cognita was made by a Drake Archmage less than two hundred years ago, and that she fought the Five Families and killed two Archmages.
Calvaron says the [Archmage] Zelkyr's Golems, led by Cognita, took control of Wistram a few centuries ago, and no one has defeated them in challenge.
Valeterisa says even the proper [Archmages] of a thousand years ago did not know her theorem, not even Zelkyr, though she adds he was a [Golem Artificer] and calls them different disciplines.
The first Cloth Golems that became String-people were made by [Golem Artificers], [Weavers], [High Mages] and [Witches], and the creation was beyond each component part.

A [Necromancer] is described by Az'kerash as standing between a [Summoner] and a [Golem Artificer], working between true imitation of preexisting beings and complete creation, and able to create something as original as any Golem with a less diverse selection of material.
In Wistram a [Golem Artificer] may create an entire Golem alone, while in Illivere Golem making is an industry run by Crafters under a Magus-Crafter.
Femithain writes the Golems' movement instructions with a fine brush, and a standard binding spell is written four or five times as large.
Golems do not have personalities and do not level, according to a character in Invrisil.
Stone Golems are expensive: even the cheapest repairable ones cost over a thousand gold pieces.
A Liscor Watch guard says a rogue [Necromancer], even a low-level one, can bring down villages if given enough dead bodies, and levels fast when that happens.
Pisces says any mage with even a single level in the [Necromancer] class is killed on sight in this part of the world.

Relc says Necromancers are dangerous and best killed on sight, asks whether you have seen a thousand zombies trying to eat anything in sight, and says that even if they are low-level and play nice he could never trust a Necromancer.
Wistram accepts necromancers as students, according to Ceria, and Pisces was expelled for what he wanted to do with necromancy.
Pisces claims necromancy is a misnomer, because reanimation is only one component of raising the dead.

Ceria says Pisces has an intimate knowledge of human bodies and that no one but another necromancer could have repaired Ryoka's shattered bone so easily, as he moved around each shattered bone and knitted them together.
Pisces says he could create a stronger undead but not a higher-level one.
Pisces says zombies are an inefficient use of mana unless used as immediate shields, preferring ghouls or skeletons.
Cervial notes that fresh human dead became zombies, and says that otherwise skeletons would be fought.
Ceria thinks a single skeleton as a guard is all Erin's mana supply could support.
Pisces casts [Animate Dead] across a distance to raise a dead Hob that fights on, unaffected by injury, until Goblins bring him down by weight of numbers.
Pisces says the price of an advanced reanimation spell is traditionally high.
Ceria thinks a skeleton that is quite intelligent means Pisces is closer to his goal of an undead that can level.
Ceria objects to Pisces's idea of creating an undead that can level, saying that if undead could level they would destroy entire nations.
Pisces proposes weaving the spells in at a deeper level, closer to how a Golem is created, using the formula Cognita taught him for embodying Golems with sentience.
Pisces holds that making a leveling undead needs the correct base materials.
Khelt's King says few can command the undead as he does, while other nations use labor less efficiently.

Small runes etched around the edges of the cupboards glow with silvery light on the cupboard holding the good food, while the runes on the other cupboards are not glowing; when Erin cuts the line of runes the glow fades and the cupboard goes dark.

Magnolia says she paid for the best preservation spells and has an [Enchanter] come by every year or so to make sure the runes are holding, while Ryoka sees tiny etched runes on the side of each cupboard.
Ceria says items have an intensity like magic's tiers, and she rates three enchanted items Tier 1, maybe Tier 2 for one ring.
A minor reinforcement enchantment is a very common basic hardening that improves a blade's strength but not its sharpness.
Pisces says magic cannot replace the actual base material it affects, so a well-forged steel sword is better than a basic enchanted iron one.
Ceria says mages have a hard time wearing magical gear unless it is made really well, since leaking enchantments interfere with spellcasting.
Ceria says enchantments on different items affect each other, otherwise every adventurer could wear a thousand magical spells.

Pisces says it is possible to enchant every piece of armor but the skill and craftsmanship needed for each piece would be extraordinary, so only the most legendary warriors have multiple enchanted items and most adventurers carry a singularly enchanted blade and ring.
A magical necklace Ceria and Pisces find resists improperly prepared food, as in Wistram's dining hall.
Hedault says leaky magical items clash, which can unleash the spells, alter them badly, or break one or both enchantments.
Hedault says it is inadvisable to touch something until an [Enchanter] has identified it, and that in this case the danger is to him.
Adventurers learn not to touch magical objects unless they know what they are, as they may be trapped or warded against theft.
Heat enchantments on blades are often simply hot, but a finer one spreads fire in a contact radius around a tree or Ogre, with non-magical flames.
An enchanted buckler emits a field about three feet in every direction that Hedault likens to a moving barrier, though a strong blow may break through.
A blade warded against physical harm and heat can ignite its tip on a spoken word with the heat contained.
Hedault says a blade melted by heat has broken enchantments that cannot be reconstructed, so its magic is defunct.
Pisces says that layering several spells on an object makes the difficulty of analysing and copying it exponential.
Pisces says an [Enchanter] could turn a piece of parchment into something as strong as steel.
Pisces adds that a spell changes when another is layered on top.
Wistram students take a class on basic enchantments and on decoding magical auras.
Fedric teaches enchantments to Wistram students and is a Dullahan.
Gazi presses her hand to the centre of a rune diagram and the runes light up, glowing faintly at first, then yellow, then searing white lines tinged with gold.

Runes on the dungeon walls light up as Toren approaches, and a cluster that turned bright green flared and exploded, blowing the skeleton to bits; runes across a hallway and on the ground are presumed to fire if touched.
Beatrice, a [Runeshaper], etches runes into her armor as personal enchantments.

The mark of [Insanity] sits on a pit wall and its magic works on those who look at it, though Ceria's half-Elven nature helped her fight it; Pisces later fills the pit with yellow smoke and shoots mud over the walls until the symbols are covered.
Pisces tells the party that, had all the [Insanity] runes been active, no Skill or spell short of Tier 7 could have saved even a Named Adventurer from the pit.
Lady Magnolia has a strange monocle with an obsidian rim and tiny runes carved into the sides that make the glass move with odd colours.
A magical mirror can be spelled for protection and to identify curses and hexes, but locked to one family.
Ryoka's market survey says enchanted weapons price between healing potions and spellbooks, and ordinary armor is cheap.
Spellbooks cost several hundred gold coins to thousands for the really strong ones.
Bags of holding hold more than their size suggests: Ryoka's holds her bed covers and two chairs, but acts as a normal bag after that.
Hedault says the bag Ryoka found holds about twenty pounds, but bags of holding rarely hold more than a few hundred pounds and those larger ones are very magically unstable.
Hedault says the same bag is superbly enchanted with no magical leakage, so a practising mage can carry it without interference.
Hedault says the fire trap spell consumed many powerful artifacts, yet the bag was unharmed.
A bag of holding may be trapped with magic far above the finders' ability to dispel.
Calvaron has a very limited bag of holding that lets him carry bottles and glasses.
Pisces carries a small bag of holding that he stole from the Golems.
An artifact is described as a wand with recharging mana and deeper reserves, and people will kill for one.
Gazi has a tightly sealed scroll with a glowing rune etched onto its wax seal, which Ryoka identifies as a teleportation scroll.
Ryoka hears of a magical service that creates horses out of magic, and it needs its mana stones replaced or recharged often.
A charm made from a dreamcatcher with metal frame and shimmering threads is worth several thousand gold and dispels magic when put against the head.
A wand with a frost spell attuned to it and a dagger with a dancing sword enchantment are used by a Wistram student in a duel.
Over half of the new Wistram students wear long robes, and in Ceria's opinion they bought them along with a low-quality wand as if it were a prerequisite for being a [Mage].
A magical charm let Ksmvr get past his gluten allergy.
Couriers usually carry magical items that ward against sleep spells.
Tombs usually carry traps, ancient curses and hexes on the lids, besides undead.
A sealed pair of dungeon double doors carries magical runes of warding with some looking like warnings.
Ceria tells Ryoka she is enchanted with something so powerful that Ceria cannot undo it, and Pisces guesses it is Tier 6 or 7 magic.
Val's dreamcatcher charm, which he says will dispel any magic on the wearer, is pressed against Ryoka's head and restores her memories before exploding.
Ceria's great-grandmother tells her that Elves were said to be immune to charms and curses, and that half-Elves keep a part of that so any spell holding one will eventually fail.
Ceria says she is going to dispel the magic now and asks Ryoka how it feels.
Ceria finds a grease spell and a shock spell set as traps outside her door, and a jet of flame disrupts the trap's fragile matrix.
A standard ward against listening exists, and Wistram students cast it for private conversations.
Ceria has heard that all spellbooks are warded against being read, and one valuable book in the room appears warded against tearing or decay.
Other students say they will talk to another mage who specialised in dispelling wards about the spellbook's magic.
Ceria reasons that whoever anchored the [Insanity] spell would have protected its runes with wards that even her best spells, [Ice Spike] or [Fireball], would fail to overcome.
Private wards on a home are weaker than a dungeon built to kill many invaders.
The wards on the Reinhart estate are sturdy; a hostile mage destroyed only one room.
Wistram's shield spell lets onlookers watch duels without risk from stray shots.
A party member says Invrisil is where people able to dispel the magic and maybe repair the artifacts could be found.
Pisces claims that anyone can obtain the [Mage] class or a variation, but they often stagnate and seldom reach Level 20.
Pisces says the lack of centralised education between nations has produced lesser variations of the [Mage] class, such as [Hedge Wizards], [Witch Doctors], [Witches], [Spellswords] and [Druids].
Pisces holds that even lesser spellcasters are unique and chosen, since they can cast spells, unlike most of humanity.
Pisces lists his own levels as fifteen in [Elementalist], eight in [Alchemist], six in [Enchanter] and ten in [Mage].
Ceria learned [Fireball] on reaching Level 18 in her [Elementalist] class, whereas without the level it would have taken a month of study and the right scrolls.
Ceria says some people believe in a Limit to levels, meaning that gaining too many levels across classes will make a person run out.
Ceria tells Pisces on the ship that she knows many attack spells and that earth and fire spells are her specialty.
Ceria says she understands cold, so spells like [Ice Spike] make more sense to her.
A Wistram student calls himself a specialist of the Wind Elementalist field of magic.
Pisces says he is no [Hydromancer] and specialises in ice magic, and adds that the air is dry around here and this is the best they are going to get.
Mages specialising in water magic warned of the weather effects of a [Hydromancer]'s [Rain] spell used in the Antinium Wars.
A [Summoner] with a wand can fire magical bolts and summon shimmering warriors that fight for the party.
Teriarch scoffs that modern mages do not know how to naturalise magic within themselves.
In Liscor people hire a [Healer] to visit with herbs and potions, and Ryoka's bandages cost about ten gold coins and had magic in the stitching, or so the [Healer] claimed.
Ryoka is told a badly damaged leg needs a high-level [Healer], or better a [Cleric], and that it would not heal on its own.
A [Cleric] is expensive and in constant demand, with thousands camping around the church in Tenbault each day hoping for one.
A [Cleric] would charge two hundred coins, or at least sixty, for a [Restoration] spell, according to a character bargaining with a mage.
Pisces says miracles are an extinct form of magic, which was a form of prayer, and that a [Cleric] in their earliest levels could do what an [Archmage] could not.
Pisces holds that miracles were a function of faith in gods and ended when the gods no longer existed.
Ryoka suggests Ceria's hand might be healed by a mage who specialises in healing and knows a restoration or regeneration spell, since there are no priests in this world.
Ryoka observes that wounds can be healed in seconds here, but all but the best healing potions leave you tired or nauseous, and the agony and shock of rapid healing can kill.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Krshia says Gnoll magic differs from Human magic: each tribe chooses a [Shaman] who wields the magic of the pack, and the tribe chooses who can cast.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Krshia says [Shamans] have no magic to cast without others to draw on, so a lone Gnoll cannot show spells on a test.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Krshia says the Wistram mages tested a Gnoll [Shaman] who asked for admission, did not believe he was a spellcaster, and declared all Gnolls magic-deficient.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Krshia says Wistram mages are not welcome among the tribes since that rejection.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Under Krshia's influence the Gnolls pooled profits to buy spellbooks of mostly Tier 1 to Tier 3 spells as a gift to the tribes, so they could train their own [Mages].

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Gnolls had never had [Mages], only [Shamans], as far as Ryoka knows.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Spellbooks are mostly immune to conventional harm, but sufficiently powerful magic will destroy them.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Teriarch says Gnoll shamans use tribal magic quite well and that Gnolls can learn magic, as some races are more adept than others.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Teriarch says the Wistram mages of two hundred years ago were no fools and wonders why they expelled the Gnoll apprentice.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Krshia says the strong Drake mages fight with their army, and magic is not widely practised in Izril.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: A Drake mage in robes stands at the back of the twenty guards at the entrance to the Ruins.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Golden inscriptions on the dungeon doors look like Drakes casting magic.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Archmage Zelkyr was a Drake famed for damaging a Walled City wall and for creating Golems.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Drake guards in Pallass track unauthorised teleports and treat unauthorised spells as a crime in the Walled City.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: In the Antinium Wars the Southern Alliance used long-range mage spells against Antinium hives, and a Drake tactician passed observations to every city-state by mage spell.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: A Drake tactician recorded that the Antinium had no mages and that this lack was a weakness.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Ksmvr thinks the Antinium have no spell casters, but they have safeguards against enchantments and illusions built into them when created.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Klbkch hears from the Listeners of an Antinium who casts magic and concludes there is only one Antinium among the living who can cast spells.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: An Antinium who glows with magic casts spells left and right in the battle, and lightning splits the sky when she raises her staff.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Frost Faeries work magic that brings winter, freezes ground and fights with snowballs.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Frost Faeries are only fuzzy blobs to most people in this world thanks to the magic they wield.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Cold iron saps a faerie's strength and makes them mortal, so Ivolethe cannot use her magic there.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Ivolethe says the fey come into existence knowing magic, so teaching it to mortals is like teaching a fish to swim.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Ivolethe tries to teach Ryoka how the Frost Faeries conjure snow and move so fast by having her listen to the wind.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: Teriarch says faerie magic accounts for more than one world and that their magics are usually broken by satisfying some rule.

section: Non-human magic: Gnoll, Drake, Antinium and fae
text: A faerie opens a door with wind without casting a spell or uttering a sound.
Moore's best spell is a Tier 5 spell, said to be one of the better Tier 5 spells in the world, and Moore of the Halfseekers reports greatly damaging the Shield Spiders' nest with a Tier 5 spell.
Ceria, who is not an expert with Tier 4 or Tier 5 spells, has one good spell and casts [Ice Wall], then raises [Force Wall], a Tier 4 spell.
Ceria observes that any Tier 0 spell could make light as bright as the Antinium's small censer glow, but that the censer's glow was not magic.
Grimalkin says [Lion's Strength] is a Tier 4 spell but, as an enchantment, could be called Tier 5, and that if he were selling it (which he is not) he would ask at least nine thousand gold pieces.
[True Seeing] is a Tier 6 spell capable of seeing through all but Tier 8 magics.

Az'kerash cannot create a scroll of [Greater Teleport] since scroll scribing is not his talent, and the black scroll he is scribing instead would sell for maybe a hundred thousand gold coins, though he does not follow the market for Tier 6 spells.
[Pestilence's Touch] is called a Tier 5 spell.
[Blackfire Fireball] is a Tier 5 spell, and holding it compressed and stable is far harder than casting it.
Osthia Blackwing says the Goblin Lord was sure his master could cast at least Tier 7 spells, probably Tier 8.
Grimalkin says most [Mages] Wistram churns out know multiple Tier 4 spells after graduating, at least three to five, though they are terrible fighters.

Pisces says linking does not let [Mages] cast spells they do not already know and can boost an existing spell several times over, as [Siege Fireball] is an overcharged [Grand Fireball], but unless the lead mage knows a Tier 6 spell or higher the effort is usually pointless.
Walls with anti-spell wards could take a few hits from a Tier 6 spell, according to Olesm's reckoning.
Falene says linked casting needs immense concentration and discipline, cannot be done by untrained mages, and in Wistram only fourth-year students and older learn to cast together.
Linked casting does not let mages cast spells they do not already know; it only boosts an existing spell.
An amulet on a Drake's chest absorbs Tier 2 spells, including lightning cast at him.
A Gnoll who was once a mage's apprentice says a certain spell is Tier 1 as mages reckon such things, low-level enough for her to cast.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Scrolls of long-distance teleportation are rarer than moon diamonds, and a powerful kingdom might hoard them for generations.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Az'kerash uses scrolls of [Greater Teleportation], each of which cannot be replaced, and says the long-distance teleport takes thirty minutes to complete or longer.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Ryoka calls a scroll the Fool is speaking into a magic scroll for talking to people.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Magnolia's message scroll is an artifact that records the messages her people deem important enough to send her directly.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Opening a spellbook page makes its symbols shine and speak in the reader's mind, instantly comprehensible, though the effort of understanding it gave Mrsha a migraine.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: One page of the Silverfang spellbook teaches a spell to conjure a stone sword out of the earth.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Another page teaches [Grow Grass], a simple earth spell of infinite variations worthy of a novice.

section: Scrolls and spell tomes in later books
text: Mrsha believes Gnolls cannot learn conventional mage magic, and that no Gnoll [Mage] has existed in living memory.
Later, Erin's staff are trained to check the magical door every ten minutes by turning its dial, and they open it to Liscor, Celum, Pallass, Esthelm and, if requested, the Bloodfields.
The door's settings later include Liscor, Celum, Pallass, Esthelm and the Bloodfields, with a glowing yellow stone marking Pallass.
The door to the Bloodfields later opens onto a hill, far from the Bloodfields.
Pallass later moves its end of the door to a chamber with a steel portcullis and eight [Guards], under an order from the Assembly of Crafts.
The door cannot send many people to Pallass: two or four per day, and the four only one way.
Garia says the door also goes to the Bloodfields and will reach Invrisil soon, with the Horns of Hammerad taking it there slowly.
A Sage's Grass field planted in the garden would generate mana that the door uses, and it recharges the door.
Hawk is told that with a Sage's Grass field the door can ferry as many as twenty people quickly and recharges fast, which he fears will hurt Runners across Izril.
Garia says Erin has a deal not to interfere with trade or the Runner's Guild, and that this is the reason she was kicked out of Celum.
Wistram keeps secret an ability to hijack a scrying mirror's spell in order to watch the person using it from afar.
Archmage Feor, a half-Elf nearly two centuries old, leads the Centrist faction and is a master of almost every conceivable school of magic.
Archmage Nailihuaile, a Star Lamia and the Revivalist leader, is known for her skill in the enchanting school of magic.
Archmage Viltach, a Human, leads the largely Human Libertarian faction and spends time in Terandria as well as Wistram.
These three Archmages held the majority of Wistram's power; Archmage is a title for the first among Wistram's Council and is not the class [Archmage].
Wistram's Council is a ruling body made up of the most influential [Mages], and not all Archmages are equal.
Wistram's [Mages] guard secrets such as their levels as fiercely as a Dragon guards treasure, and Wistram mages trade in secrets like coin.
Wistram sits on an isle in the middle of the sea within a bubble that keeps off the waves, and is enormous inside.

Within Wistram's halls you could run for hours and still not reach the other side because Wistram is magical, and many mages built and added onto it over thousands of years so that it holds more secrets and hidden spaces than anyone could guess.
Almost any powerful mage in Wistram is in one of the major factions controlling the Council or is allied to one of the big players.
Wistram has a living sand Golem that carries mana crystals in the halls.
Wistram broadcasts events as a single channel of magicvision that can show only one event at a time, and in one day it received invitations from over forty nations.

The commentators Noass and Sir Relz scramble in their studio to retell the events, and Wistram sends an apology to those angered by seeing dead children and blood, with talk of delaying the broadcast or issuing a warning.
Wistram sent a highest-priority [Message] through every Mage's Guild saying the King of Destruction had allied with Tiqr, then retracted it about ten minutes later as an error.
A High King's throne room has a scrying mirror so large that a person could pace in front of it without leaving frame.

Valeterisa was working on automated spellcasting, a theorem she calls the lynchpin of higher magic, and says creating magical dimensions is possible but rudimentary without constant management or this spell.
Valeterisa says the [Archmages] of a thousand years ago did not know the spell, and Zelkyr was a [Golem Artificer], a different discipline.
All a wand's magic is channeled through the tip, which glows or reacts depending on the stored spell, and breaking a wand triggers the spell.
Erin touches the tip of Ceria's wand and feels a first bite of extreme cold, and Ceria says she did not expect her to touch the wand tip.
Ceria's wand is held in an armband along her arm.
Ryoka learns that Ceria's wand cost half as much as her robes (nearly a hundred and twenty gold) and was a focusing agent with some magic she had to constantly renew.
Ryoka also learns one-time spells are not cheap, though a seasoned adventurer can buy some.
Octavia says mana stones are the foundation of powerful potions and that [Alchemists] used to use only them in potions since other magical ingredients were so hard to find.
Pisces suggests Octavia could brew a potion out of a mana stone, saying some [Alchemists] use them, if she could reliably harness the stone's power.
A cracked mana stone is barely worth the cost of an enchanted arrow.
Erin replaces the mana stone attuned to Pallass before the Drake steps through the door.
Nsiia's first Golem, a clay shell, ran out of power after three minutes, eating through the six small mana stones she placed in it.
Nsiia learned that a Golem needs its instruction-circuits connected at all times or parts of it stop working.
Pyrite, a Hobgoblin, keeps only the most brilliant mana stones in his collection and would call those used on Erin's door cheap.
The Mage's Guild told Erin it would not allow her to monopolise messages between Liscor and Celum.

A mage tells Erin that "mage" is the generally accepted title for all who practise magic, while wizards are arcane researchers, sorcerers are largely self-taught, warlocks draw power from other sources such as summoning, and witches practise alchemy with specialised schools.
Wiskeria says [Witches] learn many disciplines, including general magic, alchemy, hexes, charms, beast taming and even fighting Skills.
Wiskeria says [Witch] magic is more like rituals and patterns than spells, though she casts a few mage-style spells such as [Fox Fire].
Califor says [Witches] gather feelings as power and use ritual and incantation to harness it, which is less loud and forceful than a [Mage]'s spell but can do what regular spells cannot.
Eloise says [Witch] is as wide a class as [Mage], and that her own talent is tea, sociability and medicines.
Wiskeria says that a [Witch] who is not in a coven is surely a bad witch, since a [Witch]'s strength is in her coven.
A [Witch] usually meets her coven a few times a month at most and pursues her craft otherwise, Wiskeria says.
A [Witch] says that witches' magic fades, which the Gnolls call the Waning World, and that in times past witches summoned beings far greater than skeletons.
Ser Raim says Belavierr must have his hair or some possession of his to curse him, and that even then his Drathian charms work as wards and her magic is not all-powerful.
Wiskeria walks around the cauldron six times clockwise and three times counterclockwise, and the flames jump higher with each circuit as she prepares a brew.
Witches' ritual magic can backlash: a ritual's focus gem cracked and the backlash threw the witches from the circle into the river.
Pisces says older Wistram students learn to pick apart an incantation to see what is spoken, which is why he and Ceria know a unique version of a spell.
Ijvani believes that proper spellcasting with an incantation, time, material and effort is far stronger than instantaneous spellcasting.
A mage observing Ceria praises her ability to cast incantationless magic.
A [Mage] activates a spell by moving his fingers and whispering a single word, an activation phrase.
Ceria is struck by magical backlash after channeling cold through her hand, which leaves the hand numb and unable to move.
Ceria says a backlash froze her hand off when she used a spell with undead in the way.
Ceria's backlash later froze all the skin off her hand.
Ceria's wand hand burns with backlash when she casts a strained spell, and she feels mana burning in her veins.
An [Aegiscaster] whose protections were torn suffered backlash and felt the mana in her veins revolt.
Ceria and Pisces scream and collapse as their spell fails when the Creler tears itself away from the Frostmarrow Behemoth.
A filthy girl hiding behind a stall rushes into the street, hearing a whistle she thinks is for her, as her [Invisibility] spell fails.
Olesm says that an average skeleton falls to pieces within a day or two of being animated, and that even an indefinite binding fails the instant the undead takes too much damage.
A group of Wistram mages stagger with the backlash of magic after a large combined spell.
Olesm says a magical dungeon has some kind of source of mana, and Ceria says the mana in dungeons attracts nastier monsters and might make them stronger.
Ceria says magical dungeons do not run out of monsters and are far more dangerous than non-magical ones.
Ceria says the tombs were more like non-magical dungeons despite the undead.
Erin's new Skill makes the inn a place with strong ambient mana, which Typhenous calls a magical leyline.
Pisces casts [Lightning Jolt] using ambient mana in the inn while drawing minimal reserves of his own.
Ambient mana is in the earth, air and grass but is thin; Toren, an undead, burns through magic at an incredible rate and needs a strong source.
Toren can sense mana, including where it is concentrated, without having learned [Mana Sense].
An emergency escape device may not work in a dungeon's magically charged atmosphere.
Characters across the books say the gods are dead and treat it as common knowledge.
Pisces says the gods fell and no longer exist, so miracles, which were a function of faith and belief in gods, have ended too.
Ryoka's narration says the Gods fell in war tens of thousands of years ago.
Ryoka reads that no book mentions gods in over ten thousand years of history, only hints of someone trying to bring back the [Cleric] class and faded relics.
Ryoka wonders why no new gods were ever made, calling the absence a discrepancy.
Ryoka's footnote says that gods exist or existed is definite in this world, even though she does not believe in worshiping one.
Pisces recites a saying that the faith of clerics creates Gods and bridges the gap between impossibility and truth.
Pisces says miracles were an older, extinct form of magic, a kind of prayer brought into existence, such as wishing a friend healed and having the wounds close.
Pisces says a [Cleric] in the earliest levels could once do what an [Archmage] could not.
Teriarch tells Ryoka the Gods are dead in this world and the fae have more authority here, hence their control over the weather.
Teriarch says that in some places the will of the world and fate punish interference and that Gods guard their demesnes jealously.
Ivolethe believes the gods are dead and thinks they had better stay that way.
Flos says that in this world people know the gods to be dead and he has never heard of a [Preacher].
Flos argues that because he cannot ask whether a god exists while Teres can, Earth's belief suggests that some god exists there.
Teres cannot make Flos grasp an all-knowing, all-powerful being, and he finds Earth's gods more like dreams.
Narration says that there is no such thing as a [Priest] in this world, not anymore.
At the funeral for Brunkr there is no priest, no words and no ceremony, and the Gnolls lay tributes such as his sword, shield and armor by their fallen.
Sergeant Thriss says he believes in souls even if there are no gods to judge them.
Soldiers on the front call Geneva the Last Light and think her as close to a goddess as anything, though they do not say it, since the gods are dead.
People say the gods are dead, and Luan sometimes stays awake at night wondering, if they are dead, what killed them.
Narration says men gather in desperation and faith is dead, as are the gods, when a crowd calls for a small girl as a symbol of hope.
Narration says the Dragon Teriarch whispers a blessing he knows is worthless because the Gods were dead.
A Frost Faerie says that in ages past the fae danced with gods and demons and made war and peace across worlds.
Teriarch says the Fae are as old as Dragons or older and danced in a time when Gods still lived.
Klbkch says the existence of a God is tied to the Antinium's existence on Rhir, and that his original task as a Centenium relates to Gods.
Klbkch forbids Pawn to mention Gods, his class or Skills to anyone, and when Pawn asks why Gods are an issue, tells him it is none of his concern and a secret.
Klbkch tells Ryoka that the Antinium fled from a God buried in Rhir that is trying to wake up.
The Queen of the Free Antinium recalls that over three hundred Queens, most of the living Antinium, were sent to flee the sleeping god.
They left a rearguard to fight for years, expecting the sleeping god to overrun Rhir one day.
The Queen of the Free Antinium says the Antinium sent warrior-queens and their ageless Centenium, but they drowned at sea battling krakens and monsters from the depths.
The Queen of the Free Antinium says that only eight Queens survived the crossing and six remained.
Ryoka believes the Antinium fled Rhir fighting something they thought was a god.
Ryoka reads that something in Rhir keeps creating new horrors, black slime that mutates everything near it, and she thinks of it as a dead God, like Klbkch said.
Ryoka reads that a huge army from three continents went underground to find the root of Rhir's troubles and none returned, yet a year later abominations made from parts of people came out.

A summoned Earther writes that the origin of the curse on the Blighted Continent is a place where new monster species keep spewing out and that people call it an ancient monster from the time of Gods or a spell gone wrong.
Ryoka tells Teriarch that a God sleeps on Rhir and that things even the Fae fear stalk her dreams.
A character's thoughts mention a sleeping god laughing in the darkness while Klbkch regains memories.
Narration describes Crelers covering walls as a sleeping god's musings.
Narration calls Klbkch a warrior of the True Antinium who battled monsters the world had never known, dark dreams of a sleeping god.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Krshia says some people worship levels instead of Gods and in some places those with the highest level are worshiped.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Krshia mentions a belief that each person has a maximum level and that reaching it ends their life.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Halrac was taught as a lad that people return to life after death by class and level, so low-level dead return as animals or monsters.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Halrac says hell is where the Demons come from, a place in Rhir where no army has returned.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Erin tells the story of Moses, Jesus and the Christian God to Pawn, Halrac and the adventurers, and Halrac says he has never heard of one god just called God.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Pawn gains the class [Acolyte] with the Skill [Prayer] after talking with Erin about God; Klbkch says he knows of Gods only as dead.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Klbkch tells Pawn he will not allow prayer or worship of a God that does not belong to the Antinium.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Klbkch wonders whether Erin's God would accept the Antinium and whether the Antinium are its creations.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Pawn wonders what he would do if that God did not exist, whether he would obey another God, and thinks the Antinium need a God of their own rather than a Human one.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Ryoka teaches Pawn about the Abrahamic religions, and Pawn takes ideas for a shrine, prayer beads and a censer.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Pawn leads a weekly sermon and prayer for the Antinium, telling them they pray not for a god and are alone.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Pawn tells the Antinium he believes in heaven and in the worth of souls, and that if there is no place for their kind they will build it.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Pawn gives wafers to the Antinium whether or not they prayed.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Before a battle Pawn tells his Soldiers to pray not to gods but to believe in each other and in a Heaven that may exist only in their minds.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Ceria notes that the Antinium censer glows although it is not magic, which makes her wonder.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Lyonette prays for Mrsha's safety although the gods are dead, praying to nothing and everything.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Geneva prays with every stitch for her patients, because they cannot pray when the gods are dead.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Ten [Bandits] who are about to fight would have prayed, but the gods were dead, so they just held together.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Earthers argue about which direction to pray towards and whether a god exists.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Erin thinks of chess as a god who blesses and curses.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Narration says Goblins care not for gold or glory or gods, but for warm food, a place to sleep, a shiny axe and each other.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: Venitra worships her master, the Necromancer Az'kerash, without knowing what that word is; narration says if she had learned of religion she would have called his presence in her mind akin to a revelation.

section: Faith, worship and religion as practiced
text: The crypt under Liscor has prayer rooms and stone slabs, and Ceria concludes it is a crypt where bodies were cleansed, not a temple.
The Antinium believe nothing follows death; an Antinium's memory remains in the Hive and a few are kept to return in need, but they fade.
Halrac says the old teaching was reincarnation by class and level, with the higher level giving a better life.
Witch Califor says the afterlife is empty, so few ghosts remain and [Witches], [Shamans] and [Summoners] suffer for it.
Belavierr says the ghosts she summoned are old and not true ghosts, and that the deadlands are empty.
When Nanette holds her dead mother's hat, nothing replies; the narration says the afterlife was full of nothing, not even [Witches].
Wiskeria hears that real ghosts returned to walk Noelictus.
Ghosts cannot be harmed by normal weapons, as Halrac knows.
During the attack on Riverfarm, a speaker fighting beside Durene says spirits cannot be hurt by mundane weapons unless made of silver or a purifying substance like Truegold.
Revi's constructs are called from the memory of past souls, but are not the souls themselves and have no minds.
Halrac drinks ale mixed with nectar from Erin's faerie flowers and finds himself young again at home with Ariael, who died with the others.
Lady Zanthia's [The Eternal Partner] Skill conjures a ghostly dance partner who takes color and form and becomes real.
An Earther writes that gods are dead while he is surrounded by death, and sometimes he feels it is just as well.
Goblins have over twenty words for death.
Ryoka muses that hell is something you create, calling her moment at the crowded inn her personal hell.
Liscor is said to face three great dangers: rain, the undead and war.
A Crypt Lord is a dead creature animated by powerful magic that eats the dead to recover its body; its blood is black and poisonous.
Crypt Lords can command other dead and are estimated around Level 22, possibly 26, able to wipe out a Silver-rank team.
A Lich is simply the undead version of a spellcaster and is not immortal.
Undead cannot grow or change unless a [Necromancer] alters them, or they can level.
Pisces can create a stronger undead but not a higher level one.
Pisces admits he made Toren as an undead that could level, an experimental prototype.
Ruins near Liscor hold varied undead, and adventurers who vanished in them sometimes returned shuffling, trying to eat the living.
If a horde kills an entire village the dead can become zombies, but one village's zombies regenerate fully, cannot be controlled by Necromancers and guard their home.
Ghouls stream out of the zombie village and attack Rags's Goblins, one leaping at Rags and wounding her.
Zevara says the Necromancer would have brought giants, wights and ghosts.
Mage Grimalkin says he heard the basics of specter-type undead that even the current Archmages struggled against.
Toren survives a life-draining spell by stealing mana from the zombies and ghouls he commands, which fall lifeless.
Gold-rank is as high as most ranking systems go, and some countries add platinum or adamantium before the unranked.
Beyond that, adventurers whose renown is known across the region are called Named adventurers instead of ranked.
Silver-rank captains fall silent on hearing a Named adventurer, Gazi the Omniscient, is in the city, and reason she is there for the Ruins and being cautious.
Named Adventurers are living legends to adventurers with short careers.
Ryoka reasons that a Named Adventurer is only around Level 40, and so Klbkch's seventy levels exceeded one.
The narration judges a famous Drake [General] such as Zel Shivertail to be at least the equivalent of a Named Adventurer.
Amerys is called a living legend, the equivalent of a Named Adventurer.
Regrika Blackpaw, a Gnoll Named Adventurer, crushes the spirits of other adventurers just by walking through the city.
Gnolls look up to a Named Adventurer from their species as a hero.
Gazi's fame as a Named Adventurer rests on deflecting arrows and fighting guardsmen unscathed.
Venitra was enchanted to withstand spells from Named Adventurers.
Lady Xersia, a Named Adventurer called the Scorpion, became a [Marchioness] and fights only a few minutes at her best.
A Named Adventurer never loses their Skills, but age limits their fighting.
Named Adventurers must tread carefully with the Traders of Roshal, whose assassins enforce its rules.
Elia Arcsinger is known as one of the greatest Named Adventurers of the age after killing the Goblin King.
In the Goblin King's wars, three Named Adventurers charged with six [Generals]; he slew two Generals, a Terandrian [Lord] and Ironheart Calecum, the Named Adventurer.
The Goblin Lords each possessed a might on par with any Named Adventurer.
Halrac says the first adventurers into the dungeon near First Landing came out as Named Adventurers.
A confirmed magical dungeon this old draws Named Adventurers and Gold-rank teams, possibly from other continents.
A faerie tells Ryoka that names are important and not to be thrown around lightly.
Scrying needs a person's exact name or a piece of their clothing or body.
A Worker Aberration who says he is no longer a Worker, refuses to serve the Queen and refuses a name charges Klbkch and is cut to pieces.
Ksmvr says Antinium who call themselves individuals or have names are subject to fits of violence.
Workers do not have names.
A magical dungeon has a source of mana and essentially never runs out of monsters.
The mana in a dungeon attracts nastier monsters and may make them stronger.
Whatever produces the mana is usually deadly, so some dungeons are never fully cleared.
Nearby cities hire adventurers and post guards to keep the monsters on the upper levels in check.
Not all dungeons are magical; many just have magical things in them.
The tombs under Liscor were like a non-magical dungeon despite the undead.
Ulrien says adventurers classify dungeons as containment, future generations or vengeance.
A containment dungeon is built to hold a threat or a valuable natural resource, such as one built only to fight Vampires with light-based traps.
A future-generations dungeon tests entrants with traps so artifacts reach the deserving, perhaps with a map left behind.
A vengeance dungeon seals its best artifacts behind the nastiest traps and monster eggs, so that a thousand Crelers crawl out when someone cracks the lid, says Jelaqua.
Mages study which empire built a dungeon and its composition, while adventurers use the simpler system.
Ulrien says Liscor's dungeon feels like it was not meant just to hide treasure, and Jelaqua finishes that it is a huge trap and calls it a vengeance dungeon.
Pisces says a dungeon is a receptacle for the past, and even vengeance dungeons are made to hold a nation's greatest treasures.
Dungeons come in many forms, including ruined castles, old mansions or lost cities, but Liscor's is a killing field meant to channel adventurers into traps.
Pisces reports that Olesm claims even the worst dungeons hide some kind of treasure.
Adventurers owe ten percent of their earnings to the guild, and treasure from dungeons is also taxed by the city if the dungeon is on its lands.
A new dungeon can hold nothing if plundered in ages past, hold a massive fortune, or be the lair of a monster.
Diggers note that a door found in a dungeon can transport people a hundred miles, so a new dungeon's finds could be worth a great deal.
Jelaqua says she has seen cities in Baleros fall to a Silver-rank dungeon located ten miles away.
Narration says that Liscor's dungeon is not an infinite beast, it has an end and a limit.
Gazi says that to her knowledge Liscor's dungeon was only a two-level crypt filled with undead.
The dungeon near Liscor is filled with traps and rooms that keep changing and a way down that is treacherous.
In Liscor's dungeon the monsters are deliberately organized in flows, with trapped corridors and nests tens of thousands strong, plus safe spots where monsters rarely go.
Liscor's dungeon is protected against flooding; water will not enter past a certain point.
Liscor's guildmistress Tekshia declares the dungeon Gold-rank, forbidding lesser adventurers.
Before that the dungeon was not yet rated by the Adventurer's Guilds and was seen by many as minor.
The first rooms of Liscor's dungeon are a death sentence for all but experienced Silver or Gold-rank teams.
A second entrance through a rift in the snow descends over a hundred feet by rope into the middle of the dungeon.
The mace of Howling came out of the dungeon through Vuliel Drae and sold for thousands of gold.
Two Gold-rank teams report a huge artificial nest with hundreds of thousands of Shield Spiders and speculate it is a horde-style vengeance dungeon.
Liscor's dungeon contains a bath house-like pool room that puzzles Redfang Goblins.
A third dungeon entrance connects to the crypts.
The Queen's casualty report for the day lists fifty two Workers and eighty six Soldiers slain, and the Antinium have killed nineteen Flesh Worms in the tunnels so far.
The Antinium Queen wants the artifacts in the true treasure rooms but worries about freeing the guardians.
Monster attacks on the Antinium Hive from the dungeon have doubled or tripled, so the Hive loses more Workers and Soldiers than it produces.
Liscor's laws make all dungeon items technically city property.
Ceria says that in the Ruins of Albez most of the traps and all of the big monsters and guardians are already gone, because Albez was unearthed during an earthquake.
A famous magical dungeon that spawns monsters and treasure lies far north.
Geir was built on an ancient dungeon whose enchantments the Antinium Workers had yet to tunnel through.
A new dungeon in another region has drawn nearly every Silver and Gold team and unleashed monsters after breaking into an old tomb.
Liscor could charge a small entry fee and run an industry on dungeon monster parts.
A summoning ritual attended by priests, mages and aristocracy, with glowing diagrams on the floor, makes young men and women appear, many looking up from their smartphones.
The leading priest cries that the Great Heroes of Prophecy are here.
A summoned Earther says about fifty people around twenty appeared thanks to a summoning spell and were told they were the prophesied heroes.
An America Group member says all of the summoned gained the [Hero] class on summoning, none has progressed it past Level 1, and it seems to make them level up faster.
Another account says no one has had the [Hero] class in centuries.
A call between Earth people used magic that took a lot of power to make.
Ryoka says Erin and she arrived in this world and are not alone; others are scattered around.
Ryoka concludes that the levelling system was not created by someone from Earth.
Ryoka reasons that a level cap would only make sense if someone created the system, since it resembles old video games.
Krshia has never heard of someone crossing from other worlds through a spell and believes only the darkest of creatures do so.
Erin says her arrival felt like an accident, not magic.
Magnolia says the existence of another world could drive kings to frenzy and war her world would lose.
Magnolia states that Earth weapons are known but not how to build them.
Ryoka worries that people arriving could upset politics and bring firearms into this world.
Ryoka guesses she can pierce the faeries' illusions because she comes from another world.
The Antinium Queen is unaware Erin and Ryoka come from another world, and Klbkch says she would have them captured and interrogated if she knew.
Klbkch tells his Queen that another world turns upon Ryoka and Erin and that they are connected to the anomalies the Hives found.
Flos keeps the twins Trey and Teres, who come from another world, as his wards and personal attendants.
Teriarch watches the movie Contact and is one of the few not from Earth who sees the truth of it.
Ryoka tells Teriarch that two worlds are colliding and that a war of the worlds is coming.
The fae do not belong to this plane and travel between worlds.
Ryoka says faeries fear cold iron and she does not believe they can enter a place without invitation.
Ryoka's lore says never go near a faerie mound, thank a faerie, eat their food, or tell them of your child.
Faeries say they obey no one, no god, king, lord or master.
Mortals can see the fae under a full moon, by catching them dancing without glamour or by drinking the secret fae drink.
The faerie's drink is given to people trusted enough to enter a faerie mound.
Ivolethe says the fey are born knowing magic and cannot teach it any more than one can teach a fish to swim.
Frost Faeries cannot tell the future but predict it better than mortals, seeing the crossroads where mortals see only the road.
Ivolethe senses destiny and fate as threads weaving together.
Winter fae say they are old, that one of their kind perishing every thousand years would be too many.
Teriarch suspects the fae dislike attachments and debt, which is why they would refuse to help, and says they love tradition and would demand a gift for any great aid.
A faerie lady tells Erin that if the game of Gods were all it took to meet the fae, they would be long dead.
Ryoka tries to find out the faerie's name but the faerie refuses, since names are not to be given lightly.
Citizens of Liscor regard the Frost Faeries as natural forces.
Ryoka's iron horseshoe tactic works poorly against fae, who blast the person raising it.
Ivolethe says refusing a gift of goodwill on the Winter Solstice is ill luck, and that the fae govern winter, which is two thirds over on that day.
Ryoka reads that the Strygian Empire crumbled and that the Demons emerged on Rhir five thousand years ago.
Ryoka reads that the Antinium are only about a century old and appeared out of nowhere.
Rhir has always been at war, with Blighted Kings and Queens fighting new threats.
The Book of Levels was written nearly a thousand years ago.
Ryoka's narration lists legends: ancient kingdoms in the sky that fell into the sea, a legendary isle where mages gather, a maelstrom that never ends.
Ryoka concludes the age of great wars, myth and legends has ended and the balance of power has been kept.
The Dragon Teriarch changes the world just by being.
Narration mentions that Dragons fell and gods died, nothing was permanent.
The Demons hold the other half of the Blighted Continent under their own King.
The Wandering Inn has a magic door linked to other places, such as Octavia's shop.
The Horns of Hammerad found the magic door in a dungeon and brought it to Liscor.
Having the magic door does not mean the group can go off whenever they like, as a character complains.
The magic door can connect to Pallass via portal.
Goblins see the inn as nearly heaven, a place where they are safe and Rags can play chess.
To Goblins, an inn is normally death or a place to target victims, but this inn is different.
Soldiers watch the inn and allow no one in or out, magic door or otherwise.
Ryoka says her name is only a translation of a name given in another language, so a truth spell on her name did not trip.
Humans live across the entire northern part of the continent, up to where the mountain range starts, according to Selys's map.
Selys says Humans are lots of the adventurers, most in fact, though the rowdy group in question was Drakes from down south.
Selys notes that Humans do not usually sniff each other, unlike Gnolls.
Human women have a monthly bleeding period, which Gnolls and Drakes do not have.
Jasi, a Drake, says people in Celum do not like Drakes and that she has heard most Drakes do not like Humans.
Quite a few Drakes live in Human lands even though the Drake cities actively discourage it.
Gnolls and Drakes were pushed south by Humans: the Five Families destroyed the last of the northern Walled Cities and drove both peoples south past the High Passes.
The Humans took half the continent while Gnolls and Drakes were fighting each other.
Humans in northern Izril rarely owned slaves, and ladies such as Magnolia Reinhart ended it in her generation, while slaves are legal in Terandria, Baleros and Rhir.
Rhir has been at war for thousands of years, with a Blighted King as sole ruler fighting the Demon King.
Rhir is always at war and always has a Blighted King, Queen or Prince fighting some threat.
Erin Solstice, an Earther, found herself on this world after turning a corner and suddenly appearing near a dragon.
Ryoka tells Erin that other Earthers are also in this world, scattered around it.
Erin reasons that there are more people from her world than just herself in this one.
A group of about twenty Americans from Earth, summoned to this world, travels with an escort of soldiers in Rhir.
Every summoned Earther in that group gained the [Hero] class on arrival, at Level 1, which makes them level other classes much faster.
Richard tells the narrator that the King thinks the first summoned group was a mistake and wants to perform the summoning ritual again to call more heroes.
At a banquet in Rhir, Richard and most of the summoned Humans sit with Rhir's nobility while Drakes shout across the hall.
The people of Rhir know of the summoned heroes from Earth, though not necessarily in those terms.
Several Earthers realise they no longer think about their families, and Siri says she has not thought of hers even once.
Earthers compare dates and find they come from different times, with Aaron from late 2016 and everyone else from later.
An Earther reports that on Earth there are missing-people posters, airport disappearances and a Melbourne security video showing dozens vanishing.
Seven young Earthers (Kevin, Joseph, Rose, Galina, Troydel, Imani and Leon) who were in Magnolia Reinhart's care reach the inn through its door.
Ryoka took those seven Earthers' electronics and sent them to Erin's inn when assassins attacked Magnolia's estates.
Drakes are distantly related to Dragons, and Relc says Dragons are bad news because they eat people.
Relc says Drakes can breathe fire and are special because of their relation to Dragons.
Relc says Drakes prefer drier climates, warm sun and open spaces, unlike lizardfolk who live near water.
Drakes insist they are not lizards: they do not lay eggs or hibernate and are descended from Dragons only in some ways.
Selys says Drakes would not tolerate lizardfolk in their cities.
Drakes are mammals with live births and the same reproductive basics as Humans in most respects, though they call their young hatchlings.
Selys says Drakes have one male organ, not two, calling two a common misconception that applies to lizard people, while Erin says she has heard most Drakes call it the "second tail".
Drake women do not menstruate.
A Drake's tail is long, muscular and boned, can flex and twist, and can even manipulate objects.
Klbkch watches Drakes' tails and can interpret their movements almost as well as a Drake, and Pisces is one of the few Humans who watch Drakes' tails for their reactions.
Drakes have pointed teeth and long tongues, and Selys bites through beef without effort.
Drake hatchlings like to bite everything they can fit their mouths around.
Drakes in Pallass come in green, red, blue and yellow scales, some vivid and some muted, none with the pale tones of Human skin.
Olesm's scales change color when Krshia thanks him and bows her head.
Drakes eat a very meaty, fishy and sometimes insect-heavy diet and are not keen on bread, which Gnolls eat.
Drakes do not usually bury their dead in stone because it is too expensive, and usually cremate them.
Drakes do not live past seventy or eighty years on average, and those who live near or battle monsters die earlier.
Magic and potions can extend a Drake's life to a hundred and twenty years, and Ilvriss has heard of Drakes reaching a hundred and forty using potions and artifacts.
Most Drakes have no wings and cannot breathe fire, though in the Dragon age when Drakes were young they had wings.
Some Drake soldiers can still breathe fire, smoke, lightning or mist, or spit acid.
Drakes with the ancestral traits are called Oldblood, which is the correct term, and calling them anything else risks a face full of fire or lightning.
Oldblood Drakes remember a part of what it was like to be a Dragon because they have more of their ancestor's blood.
Less than one in a thousand Drakes shows the old blood, and families with pure bloodlines are far more likely to have an Oldblood child.
Oldblood Drakes are cherished, their families are often given money and aid, and having the old blood is as good as a noble title in some circles.
A company of Oldblood soldiers is called the Ancestor Guard, and one cannot join it without being born to it.
An Oldblood Drake with both wings and a breath weapon is the rarest combination.
The Flamewardens of Pallass have fire breath and the Wings of Pallass can fly.
A Gnoll in Pallass repeatedly jumps from the walls with Featherfall Potions and fails, since only some Oldblood Drakes with wings fly from the walls.
Scorchlings are a kind of Oldblood Drake whose heritage is fire within them, so most die with their mothers and survivors have flaking scales and pain.
Scorchlings are shunned.
Selys says Drakes are possessive, and Lyonette repeats a saying that if only dust were left after the world was destroyed, Drakes would fight over who had the most.
Drakes write wills to stop blood feuds over inheritance.
Selys says Drake cities fight wars against each other all the time.
Drakes have no [Kings], on the principle that no one person should be above others.
Walled Cities have ancient three-hundred foot walls, enchanted so the stone hardens and repairs itself, and no army has taken one by siege although coups and betrayals have toppled them.
Walled Cities are not all governed the same way, using an elected official, a body of powerful individuals or a hereditary leader.
Some Walled Cities are ruled by Lords and Ladies of the Wall, who are Drakes.
Krshia says Gnolls remember a time when Dragons ruled and their descendants, Drakes, built vast and impregnable cities to shield themselves from war with their elders.
Olesm says Drakes kept most of their populations behind Walled Cities and still do, only in smaller and more numerous cities.
Among Drakes a Watch Captain generally ranks with a ruling Council member and has complete authority over local military matters.
Ilvriss calls Salazsar the premier Walled City and the hub of Drake civilization.
Nelliam says Pallass is one of the Walled Cities, that it manufactures more arms and potions than any other city on the continent, and that Pallass is known for its inventors.
Pallass is built with its urban center at the lowest point, ground level, and four massive staircases rise toward the walls to higher floors with more buildings.
Pallass has magic lifts powered by mana stones.
Liscor is a small Drake city on the trade route between north and south, the only way through the mountain range besides the High Passes and coastal routes.
Narration of Selys's thoughts says justice in Liscor is harsh and swift, and its Watch is stronger than other cities except maybe the Walled Cities, and certainly better than Human cities.
Drakes in southern cities hold the Watch Captain and Council seats, while Gnolls only sometimes sit in ruling bodies such as Pallass's Senate.
Some Drake cities do not tolerate slavery.
Drakes say "Drakes do not run" as a defining saying.
Drakes do not take to magic like other species and consider it dishonourable, too easy and not military, according to an old Drake veteran.
Krsysl Wordsmith writes that Drakes do not forgive.
Krsysl Wordsmith writes that an honest Drake stabs from the front.
Drakes and Gnolls warred for hundreds of years, and Olesm believes from histories that the Gnolls were winning.
Krshia says Gnolls remember that Dragons and Drakes fought but both preyed on a common species, Gnolls, who were food for Dragons and for Drakes too.
Krshia says Drakes are stubborn and rigid, but their records let them see the past while Gnolls only remember fragments.
A speaker says Drake cities are independent bodies that do not hold hands like Humans.
The Drake cities, humbled by the Antinium, rebuilt and strengthened garrisons before 13 A.F.
Krshia is a six-foot tall furred hyena-like Gnoll whose mouth is all very sharp canine teeth.
Gnolls have no physical difference in body mass between the sexes, as Pisces notes while comparing them with Minotaurs and Garuda.
Gnolls greet by showing their teeth.
Gnolls usually say "yes" at the end of sentences and say "no" instead only when upset or angry.
Gnolls may howl only at a full moon, and they are forbidden to howl otherwise.
A Gnoll's hackles rise when angry.
Gnolls can hear four times better than a Human or Drake.
Gnolls smell when a female is in estrus or pregnant, and they have little modesty about mating because everyone can smell it.
Gnolls can smell fear, which makes leading them hard when you are afraid.

Mrsha can smell what the other Gnolls cannot: the adults have weaker noses and the children, being city Gnolls, lack the practice she had growing up smelling squirrels and rodents beneath the earth or scenting rain.
Gnolls lack periods but have estrus periods.
Gnoll mating involves a knot, so sex can last half an hour or more.
Gnolls brew a tea that prevents pregnancy.
Gnoll cubs are pretty animal-like.
Zel says it is more rumor than anything else that the Gnolls believe certain colors have meaning, and that white is not a natural color for Gnolls of any tribe.
Krshia says white fur is a mark of dire fate to Gnolls, that some claim it is a curse and others a sign of disaster, and that those who look so bring misfortune to their tribes, or so it is said.
Some Gnolls are born with white fur and others lose their colour after terrible events, and Gnolls fear such individuals.
A Gnoll calls Erin's white-furred Mrsha a cursed doombringer.
Gnolls live in tribes that wander the plains of Izril and the continent, and there are no Gnoll cities.
Each tribe has a [Shaman] chosen to wield the pack's magic.
Chieftain Nelrra is both a [Chieftain] and a [Shaman] and leans on a walking staff.
Gnolls choose who casts magic, as a tribe chooses one shaman, in contrast to Human magic.
A [Shaman] has no magic to cast without other Gnolls to draw on.
There has been no Gnoll [Mage] in living memory and Gnoll [Mages] are thought impossible.
Gnolls refuse to trade with Wistram over an old grudge.

Krshia tells Erin that nearly twenty years ago the Gnoll tribes gathered, as they do every ten years, and many wished for Gnolls to learn the secrets the Academy at Wistram teaches, which begins her story of the Wistram insult.
Later, Krshia tells Mrsha the Wistram incident was forty years ago and that her representative lasted less than a year.
No Gnoll in the tribes has become a [Mage] for at least a few centuries, before the Wistram feud, and the cause is unknown.
Gnoll tribes meet once every ten years in a Meeting of Tribes.
At the decennial gathering each tribe brings a gift or item of value to raise its voice.
Worth governs Gnolls, more than seniority or power.

Yimur says Gnolls have more of a half-language, a secret tongue used to warn each other and hold conversations outsiders are not meant to hear, and that as far as he knows only Goblins and the people of Drath have a completely different language.
Gnoll history is spoken and passed from Gnoll to Gnoll, and told differently from Drake history.
Gnoll memory says Izril was once the home of Dragons, who with Drakes preyed on Gnolls.
Gnoll memory says Gnolls hid in caverns and lived underground, and some of them changed there.
Gnolls fought Drakes for hundreds of years, were strongest in the north, and destroyed many of the northern Walled Cities.
The Gnoll population is a fraction of what it was, but tribes grow and replenish, and Krshia hints that they may reclaim old lands in a few generations.
When Gnolls make war they make it as a people and do not lay down arms until all tribes agree.
Selys says Gnolls do not like working with other races as much, and not as many Gnolls become adventurers, so the Liscor guild has not been getting as many.
Chieftain Nelrra leads a small tribe joined with other small tribes, and they are weary of Izril and of conflict with the Drakes.
Nelrra says not all Drake cities fight the tribes, but tribes fight Drake cities, are accused of thievery and feud among themselves over old grudges.
A City Gnoll is a Gnoll who left wandering the plains in tribes for a city such as Liscor, and the term is used sometimes with pity or disdain.
Rufelt says a Plains Gnoll might call a City Gnoll a domesticated fool without tribe or loyalty.
City Gnolls are free of tribe loyalty and are not born into a family of hundreds or thousands who all have connections to them.
City Gnolls are pickier about their garb, and Lyonette has met a few Gnolls who went around fully dressed.
City Gnolls are not true [Shamans], though they have tricks.
City Gnolls form secret ruling bodies in Drake cities that decide how Gnolls behave.

A City Gnoll council has no [Chieftain] but a body of the oldest, wisest, most experienced or highest-level Gnolls, and the eleven present in Liscor are described as the [Butchers], [Bakers] and [Chandlers] of the city.
