In Liscor one Gnoll representative speaks for several thousand Gnolls, and in Pallass one speaks for ten thousand.
Krshia led a large portion of the Silverfang tribe to Liscor ten years ago and leads the City Gnolls council.

Klbkch says the Gnolls in Liscor, led by Krshia Silverfang, ostensibly arrived nearly a decade ago to facilitate trade, but their true purpose was to acquire information or objects of value to improve their tribe's standing.
Gnolls eat bread, unlike Drakes.

In 5 B.F. news from Rhir had the Blighted King's armies shattered in defeat after defeat and the Demon King pushed to the brink, while the new species dubbed the Antinium suddenly vanished from the continent.
Of two hundred greatships that left Rhir carrying Antinium and Queens, only four ships reached the southwestern edge of Izril, in the last month of winter.
The history says the Antinium are poor sailors for obvious reasons and assumes they lost nearly all their ships at sea to storms and becalmed waters.
A history in the Wandering Inn's library says the First Incursion War was a decade-long war that razed cities and forced Gnoll tribes to retreat.
Antinium cannot swim or float, and they die of suffocation after holding their breath, which became the weapon against them.
By the end of the first war the Antinium had built four Hives, and a destroyed Hive left a dry desert with no vegetation or wildlife in a fifty mile radius.
Eight years after the first war the Antinium hold six Hives and a foothold in southern Izril, which are forbidden zones, and border-crossers are executed.
The history's account of the lead-up to the Second Antinium War opens in the year 13 A.F., with Izril tentatively at peace before the war began.
At one point only seven Queens were left out of what had been hundreds.
Over three hundred Queens left Rhir, along with their warrior-queens and the Centenium, to flee the sleeping god, and most drowned at sea.
Of the eight Queens that survived the crossing, six remain.
Antinium think as a hive mind, and a hundred Workers can play chess as one mind.
Pawn says the Workers felt Klbkch's and another Worker's death and remember them, since as long as one Antinium exists none truly dies.
Antinium do not level much: Workers rarely level and some never do.
Klbkch says his people rarely level, and that only the Queens level and they almost exclusively level in the [Queen] class.
Antinium lack magical affinity as a deliberate part of their creation, and since they do not level greatly magic is not seen as a viable field.
Antinium are glucose-intolerant, so pasta and bread make them lethargic and ill.
Antinium can survive freezing weather for up to two hours before needing warmth.
Most Antinium wear no clothing, and only those who go above ground wear loincloths because other species make a fuss.
Antinium recycle their waste within the Hive.
Pawn's severed stumps of three arms and one leg are growing longer, and he says the Hive has unique substances that allow limbs to regenerate and he expects to regain mobility within the month.
Antinium have no sexual organs: they are smooth chitin with only a disposal valve.
Queens produce eggs as a matter of course, which is why they grow so large to sustain a Hive's population.
Birthers are Antinium designed for one purpose, and in later years pod-like Birthers take the place of Queens in creating Antinium.
A Birther sac has no real consciousness, is designed only to create, and is fragile.
The Armored Queen has birthed more Antinium than any other living Queen and has grown huge and unable to move.
Antinium believe nothing follows death, as an Antinium's memory remains in the Hive while the Antinium themselves cease to be.
Relc says he has heard a newly grown Soldier is the equivalent of a Level 15 [Warrior] for most species, and the narration says Soldiers' carapaces are equivalent to unenchanted plate armor.
Selys says the giant Soldier types do not need levels because they are deadly enough as they are.
Pawn, a Worker, refers to himself as "this one".
Soldiers cannot speak.
Soldiers eat sitting at tables made of packed dirt because their food basins are deep and their clumsier appendages struggle to balance containers.
Selys tells Erin that she must never ask Workers what their names are because they do not have any, and the Workers go deathly still when Erin asks.
A procession of nearly a hundred Workers walks through the market to Erin, bows their heads, and the lead Worker says "These ones offer condolences to the Innkeeper Solstice."
Workers wonder whether the new game of chess is an Aberration, but decide it is not because the Propugnator did not eliminate the twelve who learned it.
An Aberration is an Antinium that is individual, rejects the Hive and kills.
A Prognugator is a leader meant to direct Soldiers and handle unexpected situations.
A Prognugator judges other Antinium, and their lives are his to use.
Klbkch becomes a Revalantor, technically above the rank of Prognugator, and can ignore even his Queen's instructions.
The Centenium are ageless champions of old whom the Antinium sent from Rhir to the new world.
Xrn, of the Centenium, is a blue-carapaced female and a Prognugator to the Grand Queen.
Klbkch says the Workers and Soldiers wear the form of Galuc the Builder, one of the Centenium.
Klbkch says that his original task as a Centenium relates to Gods and supersedes all other orders.
Custodium are partial Prognugators with natural blades, according to Xrn.
Each Hive's Queen has special dispensation to create her own unique type of Antinium, and the Grand Queen knows every Hive's secrets.
The Silent Antinium are an assassin breed with whiter, translucent carapaces, scythe-like arms and mandibles for tearing out a throat.
Two of the Grand Queen's escort are classic Soldiers whose carapaces are so heavily reinforced that they stand two feet taller than a regular Soldier, taller even than the Armored Antinium.
The Flying Antinium of Pivr have wings, though the Free Queen calls them half-baked copies of the true winged Soldiers of long ago.
Only the Silent Queen has the expertise to make her subjects so perfectly hexapodal, as with the mantis-like Xeu, while Pivr had inefficiencies in his motion.
The Antinium have a Grand Queen, a Silent Queen, an Armored Queen, a Flying Queen, a Twisted Queen and the Free Queen.
Klbkch is Prognugator of the Free Antinium of Liscor, whose Queen and Klbkch work to bring individuality to the Antinium.
The Free Queen was exiled to Liscor with few resources because her goals went against her peers.
Individuals such as Pawn, Garry, Anand and Belgrade are not true Antinium in the Free Queen's view and are tools for her and Klbkch.
Klbkch regards Individuals as more than half-made Soldiers and Workers, but not True Antinium.
Klbkch says that if he could turn a thousand Antinium into Individuals of Belgrade's or Anand's character, he would do it instantly.
Painted Soldiers are painted so each is unique, and Klbkch says the purpose is that they are Individual.
Liscor cheers the Painted Soldiers in the parade for the first time in history, with Drakes, Gnolls and Humans all applauding the Antinium.
Soldiers' names and identities came when they painted themselves.
Thaina, with Mrsha's sign language, says "I and this one would like a drink too", although instead of a proper name she just pointed.

The Grand Queen tells Klbkch that when war begins each Hive will use its Birthers to create Antinium without limit, and the silos will sustain an army twenty three times larger than their forces at the peak of the first war, for three months.
The Grand Queen instituted a practice in which each Hive improves its own designs and tests the Soldiers in practical terms, and the Grand Hive has been the most statistically viable.
Goblins are small, wiry and muscled, with pointed ears, carrot-like noses, two rows of shark-like teeth and glowing blood-red eyes.
Goblin war cries are a ululating scream that grows louder the longer it goes.
The Goblins chasing Erin generally carry daggers or short swords, with one apparently carrying a meat cleaver, and she thinks they are rusty, stained and sharp like those she met the day before.

A Hobgoblin who comes to Lyonette's table is taller than either a Drake or a Human, and the five Redfang Hobgoblins sparring outside the inn are each taller than Erin, each green, and each strong and fit.
The huge Hob leading the Goblin attack is not fat but round and made of muscle, taller than anyone but Durene, and stronger too.
Erin sees a huge Hobgoblin at least nine feet tall, maybe taller, leading a group of Hobgoblins that are all larger than normal.
Most tribes have around one Hobgoblin.
Cave Goblins are smaller, more ragged and far paler than surface Goblins, with pale green skin, glowing red eyes and hunched forms.
Goblins have over twenty words for death and treat it as a probability or inevitability.
Goblins can level but rarely live long enough to gain more than one or two levels.
Goblins that live three years or longer are only Level 9 in [Scavenger], and the highest-level [Warrior] Rags remembers was an old Hobgoblin Chief at Level 18.
Every Goblin in Rags's tribe leveled up at least twice after killing Skinner, and Rags thinks maybe it was because they fought something truly dangerous and risked everything.
As a general rule Goblins do not pick risky fights, attacking with overwhelming numbers and by surprise.
Goblins treat a lone Human traveller as only possible death, but an unwary forest of exploding trees as absolute death, avoiding it.
Goblins' offspring are always Goblins regardless of the other parent, though they may inherit traits from non-Goblin parents.

Goblins still do not have long lifespans, and Rags knows Goblins like the Gold Stone Chieftain who are over ten years old, which is old for a Goblin, yet look like any other Hob and do not really show their age.
A Goblin who is seven years old is almost old, as Goblins go.
A Goblin birthday present is living another year.
Goblins need a Chief to direct them, and wandering bands and weaker tribes are absorbed into a strong Chief's tribe.
Goblins give their Chiefs and Shamans their abilities: a [Shaman]'s spells grow stronger with more Goblins in the tribe.
Chiefs take memory from their Goblins and can remember things that happened to the tribe years or centuries ago, but only with enough Goblins.

Pyrite had guessed that if you could remember a scene you could remember a sword technique or spell, and since only Chieftains were able to access far-back memories he could not test it until his last moments, when he sent Numbtongue Skills and knowledge.
Goblins rarely speak, and in hard times they eat their dead, though none of them like it.
Most Goblins like fish more than red meat.
Goblins have a language wholly separate from Common, as do the people of Drath.
Chieftains are too dangerous for most adventurers to hunt because they call their tribe and a mob wipes out an average group.
Over a quarter of traveller deaths on the roads around Liscor are due to Goblin attacks, according to a speaker in Liscor.
Many see Goblins as vermin and a menace that must be wiped out every few years, and no one considers negotiating with them.
Goblins around Liscor include the Flooded Waters Tribe, which is the weakest in the region, and the Jawbreaker Tribe, which is small.
The Redfang Tribe's warriors are used to meat meals and lots of them.
Rags's tribe and all the tribes around Liscor allied with Tremborag and lived in his mountain.
Tremborag's Mountain City Tribe is also called the Great Chieftain's Tribe, and he is only the sixth named Goblin Rags has known.
Tremborag says he will bow to no Lord and no King.
Goblin Kings emerge every few centuries at most and each time bring destruction.
Goblin Kings, Lords and Chieftains appear to be a naturally occurring phenomenon, born out of the Goblin population with immeasurable talent.
Goblin Chieftains and Lords lead small armies and can be reasoned with, while Goblin Kings are incredibly hard to kill and lay waste to every civilization.
Goblins from every part of the world flock to a Goblin King's banner.
Almost every nation has signed a treaty to destroy a Goblin King, and Goblin Lords are actively hunted to prevent them from becoming Kings.
A Goblin Lord is one step from a Goblin King.
The last Goblin King was Velan the Kind, who as a Goblin Lord had a peaceful, trading tribe in Baleros.
In 14 A.F. Velan ascended or transformed into a Goblin King in spring, razed Zexil in a single day, and broke eighteen treaties.
Velan's army grew with every battle and his only message was the word "Vengeance".
Before sailing, Velan called Goblin Lords and Goblin Chieftains to his cause and seized the eastern ports of Baleros to build ships for an easier target.
Nine Goblin Lords sailed with Velan, including Greydath of Blades and the [Shaman] Tallis the Stormbreaker.
The Goblin Lords each had a might on par with a Named Adventurer, and the Goblin King was reckoned a match for all but the strongest warriors in the world.
Velan's crossing beat a Minotaur fleet, and Tallis the Stormbreaker killed the Archmage Balkizat in a nine hour duel.
Velan landed at Cape Heathshell and beheaded Fulviolo El and Petria Terland, breaking two of the Five Families' armies in about ten minutes.
Velan's vanguard was Hobgoblins as strong as Gold-rank adventurers, some reportedly as tall as half-Giants.
Velan killed an Antinium Queen in her Hive, after which the Antinium pulled back to defend their remaining Hives.
Velan charged alone at the mages and was killed by a single arrow through the eye.
Every Goblin on the field and perhaps every Goblin in the world sensed Velan die the moment it happened.
Zel says that when the Goblin King landed, over a million Goblins invaded Izril and the Humans still refused to run but fought, not alone, as other nations sent armies.
Greybeard says Velan was a peaceful king who ruled six years and made peace with Humans, Gnolls and Drakes on Izril and alliances on Baleros.

The Goblin Lord Osthia meets says he can sense Chieftains and other Goblin Lords as lights in the distance, more of them further away across oceans, and that there are no other Goblin Lords on this continent.
The same Goblin Lord says other Lords are dimmer and do not call other Goblins loudly, that other Goblins cannot sense this, and that he shouts and all hear although all do not obey.
A Goblin Lord's elite are thousands of Hobgoblins in looted armor, with undead doubling his army.
Cave Goblins differ from Rags's people and are subservient to the Raskghar.
The Cave Goblins treat Raskghar as their version of Hobgoblins, but the Redfang Hobgoblins find such cruelty a travesty no Hobgoblin would commit.
The word Hobgoblin is long forgotten among Cave Goblins, and when it spreads they flee Raskghar for a place with food and no pain.
Garen Redfang's leadership was a subject on which even his Redfang tribe was split.
Goblins in Rags's tribe build a wall with a gate in one night, taller than the Human village's wall.
The first Goblin baby is born in the Goblinlands, a name the Goblins like even though Humans meant it as an insult.
The Mountain City Tribe dug out a fortress that is a copy of Tremborag's mountain, in which Goblins eat and play chess at stone benches and tables.
Krshia says it is said that Gnolls dug deep to survive and hid in caverns, that some of them changed there, and that those who changed became the Raskghar.
Gnoll memory says Raskghar lost their ability to level in exchange for bodies like steel and strength beyond other Gnolls.
Gnoll memory says the Raskghar became bestial, warlike and hungry for blood and flesh.
The Raskghar are called cave Gnolls and the Gnoll tribes remain at war with them as a species.
Raskghar are huge, furred, hunched beasts larger and stronger than Gnolls, looking like a cross between an upright bear and a lion.
A Raskghar is a head taller than a Gnoll and a third again as wide, with a head too small for its body and long claws.
Raskghar use crude stone clubs and bows with poisoned arrows.
Raskghar cannot level, have no Skills and cannot gain classes.
Raskghar can bend iron but not steel.
Raskghar ambush weak adventurers at the bottom of the rift and left Gold-rank teams alone, killing eight of ten teams.

Calruz says the Raskghar are easy to command during the full moon and at other times can barely remember letters, and that only when the moon is nearly full do they regain any semblance of intelligence.
Krshia recalls old legends that the Raskghar regain their intelligence only when the moon shines, as the two nearly full moons shine over Liscor, and a Raskghar says "It is the time of hunting."
A Raskghar tells Krshia it learned the common tongue from her just now.
Raskghar have a language of their own and a camp that resembles a Gnoll tribe's camp.

In one Raskghar camp Ceria guesses there are at least two thousand Raskghar, almost all warriors, with ten Cave Goblins for every Raskghar tending fires, bringing food, maintaining weapons and butchering.
Raskghar treat Cave Goblins as slaves, eat them and throw stones at them for sport.
Raskghar had never seen Hobgoblins before.
A female Raskghar tells Calruz "Old way works. Gnolls make us stronger. Smarter. More blood means more power. All Raskghar will drink. Grow."
After Vakk is killed twenty one Raskghar stand together, and the twenty one awakened bow to their Chieftain Calruz, who says they will all bear artifacts and become his vanguard.
Calruz tells Nokha that she has done well and will lead the awakened the next day.
Calruz, a one-armed Minotaur, is called Chieftain by a Raskghar and calls the Raskghar his warriors and his tribe.
Raskghar surrender at Liscor's gates at the end, calling themselves sick and good slaves.

A speaker says Raskghar can bend iron but not steel, and Calruz says he would have explosive and Tripvine type weapons ready to throw and that no one should go near the cells for any reason unless the Raskghar manacle themselves.
Frost Faeries bring the winter, flying over the land and freezing it as they go.
Ryoka thinks that in this world winter is a product of creatures rather than weather, and that the faeries seem slow and inefficient at it.
People in Liscor regard the Frost Faeries as a force of nature rather than actual creatures.
Frost Faeries are also called Winter Sprites.
Frost Faeries look humanoid, with bodies that are part crystal and part ice and insect-like wings, and are breathtakingly beautiful.
The fairies' anatomy differs from Humans' and half-Elves': they are made of what looks like fluid ice and pure crystal.
Frost Faeries glow blue in the dark.
A Frost Faerie has wickedly sharp teeth in a tiny mouth.
Their magic makes them fuzzy blobs to nearly everyone in this world, and they cannot be heard or barely be seen, so they are generally treated like natural phenomena.
Ryoka Griffin can see and hear the Frost Faeries, which Garia cannot, though Garia still sees something.
Later, people of this world are described as looking a bit to the left of a faerie, at its glamour.
Frost Faeries delight in pranks: they throw snow, freeze hair stiff and drop frozen beetles on heads.
The faeries are called vicious, mischievous and deceitful by Ryoka.
Frost Faeries cannot stand being indoors in a building made with iron, and hiss and leap off Ryoka at the Runner's Guild door.
Iron in a home is a problem for a faerie even when invited in.
Teriarch's cave booms "Pests. Begone!" and a stream of fire blasts overhead, making the Frost Faeries scream and flee.
Faeries can be bribed with food: Erin's crepes are set out for them, and Ryoka calls them easy to bribe.
Ryoka believes, from legend, that she should never thank a faerie.
Erin invites the Frost Faeries in with a banquet, following the forms of folk stories.
A Frost Faerie named Ivolethe travels with Ryoka and is called her friend.
Ivolethe is a Frost Faerie only to the people of this world; her true nature is not Human and not mortal.
Frost Faeries cannot tell the future, but they predict it somewhat better than Humans can.
Ivolethe is immortal, and in one moment shows an immortal's distant look at the world.
The faeries are not allowed to interfere in events and risk punishment for breaking the rules.
Ivolethe teaches Ryoka faerie magic, which starts with sensing the wind.
Ivolethe can be carried by the wind as well as fly.
Faerie flowers, small yellow flowers, grow at Erin's inn and their nectar goes into drinks such as the inn's Faerie Flower ale.
Erin first received the flowers as fake gold coins, a faerie's trick payment.
Faerie flower nectar is given to Mrsha in her milk to help with nightmares.
At Laken's banquet the fae are described as fair folk who obey bargains and do not lie but twist the truth, and who are harmless if not deceived or threatened.
A fae woman bleeds on a steel blade without pain and demands that duelists bring cold iron and star metal.

Teriarch says the faeries are not from this plane of existence and travel between worlds, and that, as he is told, in some places the will of the world and fate can punish those who interfere, hence the fae keep and enforce their own rules.
A fae says she suffers a punishment from "my King" for breaking the rules.
The fae say the Faerie King does not interfere in this world's doings but remembers, and bends his rules to allow them these gatherings.
Legend says vampires are creatures of death, blood feeders and masters of the night.
Vampires are alive rather than undead, with a very slow pulse and cold skin, and see well in the dark without getting cold.
Vampires are immortal in the legends, but the Drakle family say they live into their sixties or eighties at most.
Ryoka calls vampires immortal, quick and strong, after Fierre choked her and did not flinch when Ryoka hit her.
Vampires heal fast, need less sleep, and are hard to poison.
Food does little for vampires; blood is what they need to live.
The Drakle line drink animal blood, bottled, and the family has sworn never to drink from people.
Biting does not make new vampires.
The Drakle line is born vampire and gives birth, and rarely marries outside the family.
Vampires do not sleep in coffins.
Vampires of the old days included necromancers and stronger vampires who burned up in sunlight like kindling.
Vampires have the old stories of Vampire Lords who could turn into mist and had Skills, but Fierre says she has never levelled.
Vampires cannot level, which some think was given for balance since a levelling vampire would be unmatched.
Vampires used to prey on people and control much of Izril until they were nearly wiped out.
Ylawes Byres says vampires used to be a scourge on Izril, with large infestations wiped out over the centuries by House Byres, whose silver was key.
Ylawes says vampires are gone, or no longer number thousands as they once did.
Modern vampires are sick and losing their powers, and blood of any species does not stop the decline.
All vampires long for real people's blood, and most have tried it in secret, but they live on animal blood.
Fierre, as she walks into the shadows, is described as already getting a tan.
Lady Suvelta Reinhart was known to the Circle of Thorns as a Vampire with levels who ruled Izril too long; her death was held to be the end of the Vampires.
Ylawes Byres, of the family that hunted vampires, dines with Ryoka and Fierre in Book 18, and Fierre hides from him.
Selphids are creatures that live inside dead bodies, and call themselves parasites and thieves of bodies.
Selphids are also called the body snatchers of Baleros, which is a pejorative phrase.
A Selphid inside a body shows as writhing dark green and yellow tendrils, which Erin first sees in Jelaqua's chest.
A Selphid takes on the attributes of its host, and can change bodies when one is damaged because healing potions do not work on dead flesh.
Selphid blood is a viscous orange liquid, and a Selphid can be cauterised after being injured.
A Selphid can die if it cannot get into another body after its host is destroyed.
Some soldiers say Selphids are not people.
Selphid hosts look deathly pale (Jelaqua's insides are bloodless and nearly white), and a Selphid that is not speaking breathes very rarely and blinks much less than normal people.
Selphids pay the families of the dead for the bodies they use and hop from body to body as the old ones decay, like hermit crabs.
Selphids never inhabit living creatures; doing so is punishable by death by every species in the world, especially Selphids themselves.
Selphids once inhabited living bodies and created a terrible empire, which was overthrown, and any Selphid found doing it is since put to death along with the host.
Lizardfolk say Selphids never fight each other even when hired on opposite sides, and that few remain because many were killed long ago.
Selphids are unpopular on Izril, and even less so on Baleros, because of rumours about their kind.
Pisces cites a rumour that you cannot let a Selphid into a graveyard.
Selphids are among the newly accepted Wistram students, including Drake, Human and Lizardman Selphid hosts.
Selphids work as [Guards] and an [Honor Guard] for hire in Baleros.
Selphids can pilot a body's muscles to exercise them, which Geneva thinks surpasses modern medical technology.
Okasha says a Selphid in a living body could heal it and Rampage without issue, making Selphids too powerful, and that this would lead to a new Selphid Empire.
A Selphid in a living host has full control when the host sleeps or is in dire need.
Dullahans have a loose connection between head and body and can take their head off.
A glow shows inside a Dullahan's armor when the head is off.
A Dullahan covers flesh and blood with armor, which is effectively skin.
A Dullahan can detach parts of the armor, including an arm, and the organs beneath are visible.
Dullahans prefer to cradle their heads in their hands or let them float at their side.
Dullahans' armor varies in material from wood to metal.
Dullahan social rank is set by armor, and the Dullahan in the best armor speaks first.
Dullahan features change only slightly, and they are private people who do not start conversations with other species.
A Dullahan bows his torso and then holds up his head.
Dullahans are heavy but lighter than Centaurs.
A Zombie Dullahan is a nightmare to fight because of the armor.
Dullahans live on Baleros and serve in mercenary companies there.
A few Dullahans study at Wistram.
At Pallass, Dullahans hold two seats among hundreds.
Half-Elves grow about one year to every three of a Human, and the average half-Elf dies before a hundred.
Half-Elves take on the cultures they are raised in, and many do not even like nature.
Half-Elves are gifted at magic but do not learn spells faster.
Ceria says rumours claim half-Elves are thieves who cannot be trusted and hate Humans, and that half-Elves have a bad reputation anywhere.
Ceria tells Pisces that half-Elves once ruled much of Terandria and enslaved Humans, which is a longstanding grudge.
Half-Elves are more disliked than Stitch-people.
Half-Elves and Dwarves are known for their distaste for one another.
Wistram's Archmage Feor is a half-Elf of two hundred years.
Half-Elf bodies are naturally magically inclined.
Ceria's people hold that the Elves are gone, but that magic remains in the blood of those with a drop of Elf blood.
In the oldest tales, Elves were immune to charms and curses.
Ceria's great-grandmother says even Dragons bowed to Elves as masters of magic.
Both Gnomes and Elves have walked on the twin moons.
Elves are not listed in any book of nations, though hints of them can be found.
Lizardfolk live near water, and some can breathe underwater, unlike Drakes who prefer drier climates.
Lizardfolk of Baleros are thin and reptilian, with long tails and a colorful neck frill that often contrasts with their scales.
A Lizardfolk says they are the biggest species on Baleros, look like Drakes, and are not related to them.
Lizardfolk are cautious but quite open to talk with other species.
Lizardfolk are cold-blooded, though evolved forms can gain warm blood.
Lizardfolk descend from hunters of Baleros' swamps.
Most Lizardfolk do not evolve, and most that do become Nagas, Gorgons or Lamia, from which they can change further.
A Lamia says Gorgons are huge fighters, Nagas are smaller but very strong and the usual form if there is no set path, and Lamia are small with larger brains.
A Naga has a humanoid torso on a serpentine lower body, with fins on the back of the head like a Lizardperson's frill.
Nagas wear clothes on the upper half only, and Lizardfolk admire a flashy Naga.
A Star Lamia says her glowing scales store magic, which is very good for spellcasting but makes sneaking around difficult.
The Lamia Archmage Nailihuaile of Wistram is a Star Lamia whose scales glow with accumulated magic.
A Lamia has two humanlike arms and a bipedal upper body with an agile build, unlike the larger Naga or the more imposing Gorgon.
A Quexal has feathers, scales and wings, gives up hands, is the fastest of the Lizardfolk evolutions, and is rarer than Lamia or Gorgons.
Nagas once had a settlement on Izril, and there were bitter wars between Drakes and Lizardfolk.
A speaker tells his lord that Lizardfolk are cunning fighters, and their Naga, Gorgon and Medusa forms are powerful and an asset along coasts.
Minotaurs have a bull's head with horns on a heavily muscled humanoid body, and hooves instead of feet.
Everyone knows Minotaurs are supposed to be honorable, and a Minotaur's word is said to be as good as a Knight's.
Ryoka writes that the Minotaurs have an archipelago, feud with other nations, and have tried to take over the world a few times, as almost every species has.
The Isles of Minos are a Minotaur kingdom, called the House of Minos by Orthenon and the Empire of Minos in a book Ryoka read.
A book Ryoka read says nearly a million Minotaurs are in a constant state of war and peace against an enemy to the southeast.
A pirate says Minotaurs cannot be beaten with bare hands and that their black ships are deadly at sea and on land.
Most Minotaurs do not like to use magic, so few study at Wistram.
Minotaurs are surprisingly prudish: Venaz refused to bathe with anyone of the opposite sex.
Minotaurs love military formations.
The House of Minos holds four named holdings, Maweil, Beriad, Hammerad and Samad, according to its marching song.
The Minotaur song "Home" says they were exiled from every land and found the sands of the House of Minos.
Everyone in the House of Minos under thirty years of age took part in a competition to study under Niers Astoragon.
The House of Minos closed its ports to foreign ships.
An emissary says the House of Minos is prepared to go to war against the King of Destruction.
Minotaurs march inland from warships on the dunes in Medain, uninvited by High King Perric, past the Medain-Jecrass battle, saying their foe ahead is the King of Destruction's army.
Centaurs are half-horse, half-Human, with a Human torso on a horse's body, taller than a horse.
Centaurs are heavier than Dullahans.
Centaurs dislike small spaces as horses do, and Marian is described as touchy.
Centaurs hate being ridden by people they do not trust, and might kick a head off.
Centaurs have the most complicated childbirths of the species.
A Centaur tribe on Baleros found a goldmine in the jungle and fought mercenary companies for it.
Centaurs serve as cavalry and run Centaur-led mercenary companies.
A character says Centaurs do not kill women unless in battle, even bandits.
Baleros mercenary companies recruit Humans, Lizardfolk, Dullahans and Centaurs.
A Centaur [Mage] studies at Wistram.
Garuda are bird-people covered in feathers, with a beaked face, wings that act as arms ending in talon-like hands, and clawed feet.
Garuda live almost exclusively on Chandrar.
Garuda are one of the main peoples of Chandrar, with String People and Humans.
Garuda raiders attack armies from the air with the sun behind them.
Garuda cannot simply be shot from the sky like hunting fowl, and cannot be chased down.
Garuda dislike being called birds and insist they are people, as a bat is not a bird.
Garuda in Pallass are few and far between among its Drakes, Gnolls and Dullahans, and they hold no seats on the city council.
Bevussa Slenderscale was abandoned as a chick and raised by Drakes in Pallass, which gives her a Drake name.
String People, also called Stitch-People, have bodies of cloth and can reattach limbs, change eyes or redesign themselves given the right materials.
A String-Girl says she feels sensations like a Human, can change her body within limits, and burns easily.
A String Person dies if too much of the core is removed, but over time can replace every part and still be herself.
String People need bones and organs, and shaping a body like another creature can go horribly wrong.
The fabric matters: cotton is normal, wool or rougher cloth for the poor, canvas makes heavy rough people, and silk would be very costly.
Skin tone comes from the fabric chosen by the makers.
String People are widely accepted, though some people are unsettled by them.
String People are one of the main peoples of Chandrar, appearing human until the stitches show.
String People are supposed to be fearless warriors, and veiled Stitch-warriors with spears call Flos their King.
String People value their own highly.
A confederation of String People nations lies to the south of Chandrar.
Their home is the Empire of Sands, one of the String People's greatest empires.
Demons are mutated Humans and other species with their own civilization and army, one of three powers in the Blighted Lands.
Demons vary in looks: some have wings, talons and beaks, others look nearly normal apart from small differences.
The war between Humans and Demons has lasted a thousand years or more.
A Demon seen by Tom has bright yellow eyes, ram's horns, fur and four toes.
Tom thinks Demons are ordinary people with skin conditions who fight as a team.
The Demon King uses fearless Demon soldiers who do not fear death.

An unnamed speaker infers that the Demons reached the Blighted King's castle by teleportation magic, a scroll and possibly artifacts, for which the Demon King must have used every magical item he had.
The Demon King commands powerful Skill users and Deathless.
Demons are weaker than they were a century back, and the world's armies once assailed them without ending them.
The Blighted King regards the Demons as an obsession and a curse.
Demons are described by one character as a folk with whom Drowned Men, Dullahans and Drathians trade.
Demon flying forces ambush unprotected patrols, and a [Demon Huntress] warns that patrols need heavy archer or [Mage] cover.
Harpies were an indigenous people of Izril, with a nation of their own, and are now believed dead.
A Gnoll remembers his tribe trading with Harpies who once ruled a large part of Izril.
Harpies are smaller than Bagrhavens, use armor and Skills, and have no hands.
Most Harpies died out, and the rest joined the Demons.
Giants once walked Terandria and every continent, taller than castles, and their blood is fading in their descendants.
The true Giants of old are classed with Ogres as sub-races that cannot level.
A half-Giant eats three times as much as other diners.
A person with a quarter of a Giant's blood is hard to feed and to find a bed for.
Half-Giants have skin like armor, especially those in whom the blood runs strong, and the shortest of the half-Giants among the Nomads of the Sky are nine feet or more tall.
Half-Giants do not need to eat as often as other people.
Half-Giants are called people overgrown, far more civilized than Ogres.
The Nomads of the Sky are one of the last groups of half-Giants in the world and are welcomed by Flos.
A half-Giant says half-Giants are greater than the smallfolk and are not gentle.
Dragons, Giants and Djinni have almost left the earth.
Ogres are humanoid but monstrous, more intelligent than Trolls, and can be reasoned with and use tools.
Ogres do not multiply like Goblins but grow fast.
Ogres are classified with monsters such as Trolls, Goblins and Giants.
Ogres have no ability to level, though some rule over Goblins or enslave other species.
Ogres have little magic, but an Ogre Shaman can gain magic by drinking up to a hundred potions slowly.
Talia reasons that if half-Giants, or rather quarter-Giants, are what Gnolls are, capable of leveling and classes, then Ogres are what the Raskghar are.
Dragons are immortal and cannot level.
Dragons have innate magic beyond any [Mage]'s, scales that deflect arrows, and can fly and transform.
Dragons bear few young, and their young age very slowly.
A young Dragon is considered an adult able to leave at two hundred years.
Dragons can sleep for long periods, even a decade at a time.
Dragons have bony spurs for eyebrows, and speak.
Ryoka, observing Teriarch smile, thinks Dragons are conceited, prideful and not a little susceptible to flattery.
Dragons are greedy and possessive about their hoards.
Dragons are touchy and dislike losing.
Dragons are formal and mark milestones such as a two hundredth year.
Dragons sustain flight with magic.
Drakes are distant cousins and descendants of Dragons.
The Walled Cities were constructed in the age of Dragons.
Dragons once ruled the world but were overthrown, chased back to the Walled Cities and exiled by their children, the Drakes.
Dragons are almost extinct, and one is slain only every few thousand years.
Only two Dragons remain on Izril, one of them a young woman raised in Manus.
Wyverns are inbred cousins of Dragons that, unlike Dragons, lack speech and vast intelligence.
Drowned People are a race created when parasites from the ocean fused with Humans or other species.
Many are peaceful, products of an accident, but others are pirates.
Pirate raiders of Drowned People wear red bandanas.
Seborn has half his face covered in crustacean shell and a crab-like claw hand.
Both Drowned Men and Drowned Women exist.
Seborn is said to smell like fish.
A character says Drowned Men and [Pirates] trade with Demons.
Beastkin are not to be confused with Gnolls, though both live around Liscor.
Beastkin come from another continent further south, and are peaceful and easy to work with.
Beastkin have tribes named for animals, such as the Long Ear Tribe (rabbit), the Jackal, and the Squirrel tribe.
The Squirrel Beastkin Foliana has odd eyes and tends to blend into her surroundings.
Hawk, a Rabbit Beastkin, is a giant talking rabbit who works as a Courier of Liscor.
Gazers have 360 degree vision.
Gazers can cast spells as easily as looking, as can a half-Gazer.
Gazers keep to themselves and are rarely in Centaur-led or Dullahan-led armies.
A half-Gazer (Gazi) has one large central eye and four other eyes.
Fraerlings, also called the Small Folk, average about a Human hand in height.
Fraerlings are a reclusive people of Baleros who mostly stay within their communities.
Fraerling walkways are enclosed to protect them from birds and rodents.
Niers Astoragon is the most famous Fraerling in the world.
Djinn are a highly magical, part-spirit people thought dead.
Djinni are almost pure magic and are exceedingly useful, though dangerous to face.
A djinn bottle grants wishes, but wording must be exact.
A Djinni can be enslaved and bound by word-bonds, as one is as driver of the Unmarked Coach.
Djinni are difficult to manage.
Djinni are the servants of Merreid.
Dwarves live in Terandria, though they once lived everywhere.
Dwarves are hidden in the heart of mountains.
Dwarves are short for a Human, about five foot two for a modern Dwarf.
Dwarf smiths are good [Blacksmiths] with pure steel, and Dwarven-made arms vary in quality.
Dwarven crossbows are made with very fine craftsmanship.
A Dwarf fought at Liscor with other peoples.
Elves, Harpies, a djinn-like people and undead kingdoms are all gone, and Dragons are mostly dead.
Halflings once got blamed for human thefts "until the small folk passed".
The Centenium were one hundred Antinium whom the Grand Queen gave individuality, names and strength, made to be heroes.
Only three Centenium remained at one point.
Klbkch was one of the Centenium.
A Shield Spider is a huge spider whose silver-and-black plated carapace covers its legs and body like armour.
A large Shield Spider stands nearly half as tall as a grown woman.
A Shield Spider clicks its mandibles as it approaches prey.
Shield Spiders lair in large underground nests full of egg sacs, covered by a pit trap of false ground made of dead grass and sticks.
One large spider will hunt a single target steadily while the rest of the nest keeps swarming around its eggs.
An adventurer watching Erin's burning pit says Shield Spiders are notorious for tracking and killing prey across thousands of leagues.
A thrown rock does not crack a Shield Spider's armour.
Acid pits a Shield Spider's armour but does not stop it, and Rock Crabs and Shield Spiders are described as mostly immune to acid flasks.
Shield Spiders have a decently strong venom.
A single Shield Spider is called a Silver-rank threat, and a nest might bring out a team of Gold-rank adventurers.
Shield Spiders cannot be tamed unless the tamer has the [Beastmaster] class.
Shield Spiders are weak against fire, and a nest can be burned with [Fireball] spells and shield-bearers.
Shield Spider carcasses do not burn up in flames, so they can still be claimed for the bounty.
The Adventurer's Guild pays an average of eleven pieces of silver per Shield Spider slain and pays more for the bodies.
A [Blacksmith] with the right skills can make shields and armour from Shield Spider bodies.
Most adventurers who are not Silver-rank or higher would rather run than fight a Shield Spider.
Erin Solstice earned just over eleven gold coins from the bounty and the carcasses of the nest she killed, less because some were burned too badly to use.
Shield Spiders normally come in nests of at least fifty and as many as three hundred.
Antinium Soldiers can crush a Shield Spider nest by leaping into the pit and stamping the spiders and eggs to death.
Shield Spider nests are pit-trap lairs that lure in prey as food for the winter.
A Shield Spider crawls up over the edge of a collapsed snow-covered nest pit and Relc kicks and pokes it back in.
Shield Spiders bite at a skeleton and web it up until they realize there is nothing to bite.
The Broken Spear Tribe's Chieftain wears armour made from Shield Spiders, as does much of his tribe, and they have even managed to tame the spiders.
A Goblin commander rides a vast Shield Spider into battle against Humans at Esthelm.
A Shield Spider ridden by a Goblin commander is smashed into the ground and killed by the Redfang Hob Grunter's axe blow.
A market seller advertises a Shield Spider trained by an expert [Beast Master] as invaluable protection.
Shield Spiders in a deep nest can be bigger than Rock Crabs.
Crelers tear Shield Spiders apart, since the spiders' bites do only superficial injuries.
A dungeon room hides a mile-deep pit of Shield Spiders, some the size of a house.
A Rock Crab hides under a boulder-like hollow shell as tall as two people and as long, and lifts the shell to scuttle on countless legs.
Its pincers are long and dark brownish orange, and it makes a loud clicking like gunshots as it runs.
A Rock Crab gives up a chase after a while and wanders back across the plains.
Rock Crabs are seen in a herd, and Erin drives two of them off by pasting their shells with slimy seed cores, which makes them retreat with loud clicks.
Erin Solstice believes a Rock Crab could level her inn.
A Rock Crab wandering slowly across the landscape ignores Erin and her skeleton as they stand back and watch it.
Goblins kill a Rock Crab by swarming it, clinging to its shell and crawling underneath, and eat its guts and bitter flesh.
Rags and a group of Goblins kill a Rock Crab from inside its shell, stabbing up through the carapace, and the crab's eyes are called pathetic.
It normally takes around twenty Goblin lives to bring down one Rock Crab, but the meat feeds the tribe for about a week.
A Rock Crab is near-certain death for one Goblin or a small party, but only many deaths for a tribe.
Rock Crabs look like snowy mounds in winter and can be camouflaged by snow until they strike.
Sending a melee group against a Rock Crab leaves red smears unless the adventurers are very high level.
The Rock Crab is an apex predator of the plains, and it preys on Corusdeer, sheep and goats.
A Rock Crab avoids large Shield Spider nests and hides in spring from predators that snack on it.
Klbkch advises Pawn that Rock Crabs should be engaged with caution if it becomes necessary.
Rock Crabs are still seen on the Floodplains of Liscor in Book 7.
A Corusdeer is an oversized reindeer with orange-brown antlers and sooty marks on its fur.
A Corusdeer's horns glow until they are nearly white with heat, and it charges with an explosion of fire that makes it much faster.
A wounded Corusdeer that runs out of energy stops glowing and becomes just a tired reindeer.
Corusdeer and Snow Golems are natural enemies.
Corusdeer move in herds, and a herd's glowing horns turn an incoming wave of snow into steam.
A Corusdeer herd can incinerate even the most dangerous enemy in seconds, and Rock Crabs are no threat when many deer are together.
Klbkch advises Pawn not to engage Corusdeer herds if at all possible, since they are formidable combatants if roused and the Soldiers would suffer heavy losses.
Driving a Corusdeer herd away from Liscor is a public boon, especially to travellers on the northern road.
Corusdeer meat is the local specialty near Liscor, served as ragu and as steak.
Corusdeer soup made by Erin stays warm to the touch and is magical.
Erin says she tried to show Agnes how to make the Corusdeer soup, but Agnes could not do it even when she copied Erin exactly.
Octavia says a blaze bomb is made with the scales of an Ignition Salamander and Corusdeer horns.
Octavia says she has found a way to blend a tiny bit of Corusdeer horn with sulfur, and a match made this way bursts into flame when struck.
Corusdeer horns once crushed the bones of the skeleton Toren, though they regrew.
A hatchling Creler has long spider-like legs with barbs, a squat elongated body, a red and purple carapace with exposed organs, and a maw of circular teeth.
Hatchling Crelers resist swords because their chitin is hard, so blunt weapons such as a mace work best.
In the larval stage a Creler looks like a fat, red, faintly glowing caterpillar and is far weaker, until it turns itself inside out into its attack form.
Larval Crelers left alone for a few months with food may become adults, which even Gold-rank teams do not want to fight.
An adult Creler is far larger than a hatchling and can fly, and it takes many Soldiers to bring one down.
Crelers are not a valid food source, because their eggs may incubate in the body of anyone who eats them.
An adventurer says the bounty on Crelers is known to be large and that they hear killing an adult carries a two thousand gold coin prize.
Crelers lay orange and red eggs in the bodies of their dead victims.
Crelers have an orange glowing body inside black and bloody red chitin, and their toxins poison those they wound.
Crelers are viewed as a threat to all species, created rather than born of this world, and animals ally against them.
Falene says even non-violent animals attack Crelers and a nest systematically wipes out all life in an area before colonizing a new location.
Hatchlings and baby Crelers can be managed by Silver or Bronze-rank teams if the nest is small, larger nests and juveniles match Silver-rank teams, and adults are a threat for any Gold-rank team.
In Baleros, three Gold-rank teams were once sent together as suppression teams against really big Creler nests.
Crelers are described as a product of the blight that afflicts Rhir, and for eight hundred years the Blighted Kingdom fought the Creler Wars.
During the Creler Wars over eight hundred Silver-rank teams killed Adult Crelers, and the first Blighted King was one of the individuals who passed Level 80.
An Adult Creler speaks without words into the mind of its prey, in the same language as Skinner, and gloats at Yvlon.
The Silver-rank Horns of Hammerad are hailed as Hell's Wardens after they kill an Adult Creler.
Face-Eater Moths are large insects that the dungeon houses, so big that one has to crawl down a tunnel.
A dungeon Face-Eater Moth can rip off a Soldier's arm and bury its mandibles in another victim.
Yellow Splatters holds the opinion that a powerful monster such as a giant Face-Eater Moth or a Crypt Worm would quickly kill regular Soldiers.
Bird counts Face-Eater Moths among the things that are not birds and are threats, with Rock Crabs and Shield Spiders.
The adult moth is furry with a long body, huge wings with a staring pattern of black spots on brown chitin, and a razor-sharp mouth.
Thousands of smaller carnivorous moths cling to a giant moth and fly up in a swarm that covers the sun.
A giant Face-Eater Moth is larger than Erin Solstice's inn, and one wingbeat sounds like thunder.
A giant Face-Eater Moth bursts out of a rift in the Floodplains in a geyser of water and dries its wings before the swarm takes flight.
A report from Salazsar describes a swarm of Face-Eater Moths with individuals exceeding forty feet in height.
Noass says that apparently the exceptionally large moths are brood mothers that lay thousands, even tens of thousands, of eggs.
Tens of thousands of Face-Eater Moths flood the walls of Liscor and claw at the city's magic barrier.
The moths cover the sky above the Floodplains and crawl over windows of the inn.
When Guardsmen loose arrows at a group of Face-Eater Moths, the hit moths fall to the ground and wriggle, some still alive.
Klbkch warns that insectile monsters survive eradication by letting their young infest new sites, so a city must clean up bodies after battle.
Klbkch says the water will eradicate the young outside the walls, as will local wildlife.
Some Face-Eater Moths flee Liscor and form a colony in the slopes by the Bloodfields.
Three Silver-rank teams, including Thunder's Solace and the Horns, fight the Bloodfields moth nest with spells and arrows.
Hissle insists on full extermination of the moth nest because Face-Eater Moths can dig.
Eater Goats are monsters of the High Passes, a match for a Carn Wolf, deadly, quick and fearless, and they will eat anything.
An Eater Goat's jaws can crunch stone or metal, and the goats hunt in packs.
They are considered a terrible threat worthy of a Gold-rank team.
An Eater Goat bites and does not let go until it has eaten its target or died.
An Eater Goat can stay on its feet with eight arrows in its side.
An Eater Goat bites a thrown fire vial in mid-air and explodes, scattering the herd.
Eater Goats are bigger than normal goats, with wide yellow eyes and jaws that rend steel.
Eater Goats refuse to die, multiply with supernatural speed the more they eat, and charge into a wall of pikes to eat.
Eater Goats are low on the food hierarchy of the High Passes, since Gargoyles and Wyverns can prey on them.
Eater Goats scream like a chorus of the damned and ram a village gate with their curved horns.
Redfang Goblins who paint their faces and bodies red are treated as not-Food by the Eater Goats.
The Redfang Goblins follow the goats south for protection against Shield Spiders, Mothbears, Armored Crawlers and Wyverns.
The goats rest after a feast until their systems work through the meal.
Thousands of Eater Goats charge a Human force from the side and ignore spells and arrows, and horses do not do well against them.
About a hundred Eater Goats gather behind a hill to attack Goblins in a valley.
Wyvern meat is a delicacy.
Hawk warns that the white Wyverns come down from the mountains sometimes and love the cold.
A Wyvern can dive incredibly fast, so travellers who see something overhead should find shelter.
A Wyvern is a humongous beast, nearly three times as tall as Ryoka Griffin, a lesser Dragon without claws and with dark purple scales.
A Wyvern can grab even an adult in seconds.
Frost Faeries can freeze a Wyvern in seconds.
A weyr of nearly a thousand Frost Wyverns, led by a Wyvern Lord far larger than the others in his clutch, flies out of the High Passes.
The average adult Wyvern is thirty to sixty feet from head to its long serpentine tail.
Wyverns hate bugs, and the Wyvern Lord passes Liscor because it is too small.
A Dragon drove the Wyverns from their challenge to his territory in the High Passes.
The Wyvern Lord senses magic and a Dragon-like aura from Pallass, and few monsters stray near it.
The Wyvern Lord turns on Pallass to claim a nest.
A Greater Wyvern is practically impossible to kill with magic, and no one below Level 30 will tackle it.
Massed Skills throw the Wyvern Lord back when Gold-rank adventurers and elite Soldiers charge it.
Ashfire Bees withstand heat and start fires when gathered in groups, which is most dangerous in spring.
Octavia says Ashfire Bee honey is not the best of reagents, but she can see it acting as a potent base, though this is not confirmed.
Bird says the bees Erin cooked, called Ashfire Bees by Octavia, are considered a Gold-rank threat and practically impossible to kill without mages.
A bee hive in a cave is not calmed by smoke, because Ashfire Bees scatter and extinguish the fire instead.
Ashfire Bees can patrol twenty miles around their hive and return together when the hive is in danger.
Ashfire Bees fly at thirty miles per hour, faster than a honeybee or a hornet.
Ashfire Bees follow the instinct of finding an intruder and stinging it, and a hive is led by a queen with workers and drones.
Selys says the Guild ranks Ashfire Bees as a Silver-rank threat, but that a hive is dangerous even though a lone bee rarely attacks anyone.

The Horns of Hammerad take Watch Captain Zevara's Ashfire Bee nest request, and the Silver Swords and the Halfseekers go along, apparently to watch, which Maviss calls two Gold-rank teams for a bee nest.
Apista is an Ashfire Bee twice the size of Ryoka Griffin's hand, kept as a pet by Lyonette du Marquin, who says she has a lesser bond with her.
Apista bursts into flames and jets fire from small holes in her body, scattering the bees around Lyonette.
After Apista stops stabbing the tired queen and circles with her, Klbkch believes Apista has just claimed her territory in a queen's battle turned into a hive's dispute.
An Acid Fly is a beetle-like insect with four legs, a black body and a glowing green abdomen.
Flicking an Acid Fly makes its abdomen burst in a splash of acid that burns skin.
Only the male Acid Flies carry the acid, which they use to dissolve dead flesh into a syrup for themselves and the females.
Acid Flies are a local creature near Liscor, and Drakes and Antinium eat them.
Erin's acid flasks of pure Acid Fly juice sell at twelve silver coins each, and Lyonette says she is told one can kill a Ghoul in less than a minute.
Acid Fly juice melts organic material in seconds but not glass or metal.
A Razorbeak is a giant pterodactyl-like bird with leathery wings and a beak longer than a person's arm, light green with red markings.
Erin finds a foul-smelling nest in the grass holding grisly remains, which she takes to be the normal birds eaten by the dinosaur-birds.
A Razorbeak's egg is about three times the size of a normal bird egg.
Razorbeaks have beaks full of teeth, bite at people, and a Razorbeak dives at and pecks Erin when she grabs its eggs.
Razorbeaks come to feed on carcasses and entrails in a fight and bite at those nearby.
A Razorbeak tries to lift Mrsha, a Gnoll child, and carry her away.
A Razorbeak is killed with a thrown kitchen knife.
Bird shoots eight Razorbeaks with arrows in one hour.
Razorbeaks are seen in the air over Liscor's Floodplains.
Carn Wolves are giant rust-red wolves of the High Passes that like to sneak up and kill Goblins.
Ryoka Griffin first judges a Carn Wolf to be only about twice as big as a normal wolf, with rust-red fur and visible muscles.
Rags judges Carn Wolves to be at least three times as large as a regular wolf and able to bring down a horse in a single strike.
Carn Wolves are deadly enemies to Goblins, but the Red Fang Tribe rides them as mounts.
A Red Fang rider's Carn Wolf crunches a Goblin in an instant, and the mounts do not flinch at a crowd of Goblins.
A pack of Carn Wolves hesitates when many smaller enemies face it.
An adventurer guesses the 'goats' are probably the flesh-eating kind with sharp teeth that can tear even Carn Wolves apart.
Bear traps are said to be useless on Gargoyles and Eater Goats and maybe useful on Carn Wolves.
The Redfang Tribe at the base of the High Passes often clashed with Eater Goats, Gargoyles and feral Carn Wolves, monsters as dangerous as the Raskghar.
Gargoyles are described as the most prevalent type of monster in the High Passes.
A Gargoyle looks like a boulder until it unfolds stone wings, and it has a hulking body like a bird crossed with an ogre.
A Gargoyle's skin looks like stone but slides around like flesh, and it has a curved beak-mouth.
Gargoyles fire stone fragments from their mouths like a shotgun.
A Gargoyle pulls a goat apart and crunches the pieces, and its spat stone fragments eviscerate a wolf.
Gargoyles have a sense of smell.
Gargoyles hide in plain sight in the High Passes, camouflaged as rock.
Gargoyles are harder for Redfang Goblins to fight than Eater Goats.
Redfang Goblins tie an Eater Goat to a pole to lure Gargoyles.
Ceria Springwalker notes that no Gargoyle is carved to look like a beautiful woman, so a stone woman must be a Golem.
A Crypt Lord threat can wipe out a Silver-rank team, with an estimated level around 22 and possibly 26 with special abilities.
A Crypt Lord is a reanimated dead creature that has grown more terrible over the years, stands taller than every adventurer present except Calruz, and eats the dead to rebuild its body.
A Crypt Lord has poisonous black blood that carries disease and death.
Crypt Lords can think and command the other dead.
A Crypt Lord spits poisonous black blood across a moat and kills Antinium Workers.
A Crypt Lord's mind presses the command DEATH on Toren, and it beats him to pieces after he stabs it.
Unburied dead at the site of a battle rise as zombies, then skeletons and Ghouls if the slaughter is great enough, and given time stronger undead such as Crypt Lords.
A Ghoul crouches on top of a victim slashing with its claws, and a dagger rammed through its softened skull into the brain does not kill it.
Acid dissolves a Ghoul.
In one famous village the zombies do not move from their former home, regenerate and reattach limbs when killed, and no [Necromancer] can control them.
Ghouls come out of the zombie village after the zombies, and a Ghoul impales itself further on a blade to keep fighting.
Crypt Worms are the smaller, weaker versions of the monster Skinner, and they bring zombies, skeletons or Ghouls to attack the Antinium.
A Draugr is a higher undead, akin to a zombie but fast and tough, which only a truly high-level [Necromancer] can animate.
A Wight is another undead type, whose touch paralyzes.
The undead that enter the tunnels for the Goblin Lord's army are mainly zombies, a few skeletons, Ghouls in small packs and a handful of the deadly Draug.
Undead Goblin children explode when killed, and early blasts kill dozens of defenders.
Over a hundred thousand undead, maybe closer to two hundred thousand, surround the inn, and adventurers kill them by the thousands each day.
Stone Starers are monsters covered in a thick stone shell, with only a front resembling a black eye with a white pupil exposed.
A Stone Starer has long wiry arms of the same stone shell and shoots beams from the white hole in its front.
The beams pierce weak enchanted metal and steel with ease, so attacking from the front is dangerous.
Stone Starers are midriff-high, and a pickaxe blow to the head kills one and spills grey-blue blood.
Stone Starers can be evaded, unlike Crelers or Rockmites, and their magical eyes are a product of magical gemstones.
A Stone Starer nest makes the Miners pull back and call in adventurer teams.
A Snow Golem is a snowman, built by a Drake child, that gained life from magic and is hostile to everything living.
A Snow Golem grows by absorbing snow until it is taller than a Rock Crab and just as wide.
Stones caught in its body can overheat and explode when a Corusdeer's glowing antlers touch them.

Snow Golems twice Erin's height bite with sticks for teeth and their packed snow resists her blows, but she realises a shovel is what she needs, digs herself out and takes her Golem apart with little trouble.
Hawk warns that Snow Golems are practically invisible in the snow.
A giant Snow Golem about two hundred and sixty feet high makes the Redfang Warriors race away.
A Krakk tree struck by a thrown rock explodes its upper branches, twigs, acorns and bark outward like a shrapnel bomb, leaving the pale yellow-green-white trunk denuded of bark.
They do burn well, but they often explode and the shrapnel is deadly.
The bark explodes about thirty seconds after being heated by fire, but rolling the wood or cold does not set it off.
Exploded bark leaves a crater-like blast in the snow around the wood.
Dropclaw Bats are meat-eating bats twice as large as a human's head, with sharp claws, that drop on a victim's head.
In a cavern three Goblins die to the bats before Rags's fire panics them.
Wailer Frogs make incredible noise that can deafen and shatter glass.
They are big enough to eat some people whole, leap powerfully, and can paralyze or deafen with their scream before swarming their prey.
The adventuring team Pithfire Hounds loses all its potions to Wailer Frogs and its horses are all dead, so it flees on foot toward Reizmelt from near the Gilliel Swamplands.
Giant snakes rest in a dungeon, fat and gorged on prey, and the largest one swallows an adventurer whole after striking.
Nets hold giant snakes while warhammers and axes finish them off.
A Sea Serpent is a massive creature of the sea whose scales shrug off arrows and harpoons.
A Vorepillar is a cowardly caterpillar plague made by a Deathless of the Demon King.
The Vorepiller does not evolve, reproduces faster than any species and is so inedible that other insects and birds will not eat it.
Drassi says Fortress Beavers are really placid animals unless their dams are broken, and a real threat when it rains since they like to create huge forts.
A Fortress Beaver is larger than a young Gnoll girl and chatters wary warnings.
Fortress Beavers fight Crelers beside Shield Spiders, then smash every Creler egg.
Mothbears are bears that can kill any other intruders into their domain.
Redfang warriors kill six Mothbears and skin them to eat.
The narrator says a Mossbear is a bigger, tougher bear subspecies, though Mothbears are even more feared.
Mothbear flesh is eaten by Goblins as a stew ingredient.
In a Drake child's story, a hero's sword slays a Mothbear, a Wyvern and a horde of undead.
Hunters must make sure bears they hunt are not Mothbears.
A herd of wild boars is led by an alpha through the snow and forages for food in winter.
Boars are weak individually, but together their tusks and explosive power can gore all but the deadliest enemies.
A grey wolf pack that is not Carn Wolves circles Erin Solstice when she sings, and she fights it with [Minotaur Punch].
A faceless leathery monster with long talons and barbed forearms is killed on the plains.
A huge slime rears twelve feet tall with colored swirling sections and engulfs a Hob whole.
A slime repairs damage from spells with purple gathering at the wounds.
A Goblin tribe fights a slime for thirty minutes and loses many.
A colony of Metalbite Slimes waits at the bottom of a fifty-foot pit trap in the dungeon.
A magic healing slime can mend wounds, and eats dead Crelers.
Skinner's body is layered dead skin, a slug-like bloated torso with two massive arms that drag it along, no legs, and two ruby eyes in a sunken face.
Skinner builds his body from entire skinned bodies, including the faces of the adventurers he kills.
The sight of Skinner leaves Ceria Springwalker unable to move or lift her wand.
Skinner leads hundreds of dead out of the Ruins of Liscor in an invasion directed by a single creature.
Something invisible touches the guards manning Liscor's gates and they throw down their weapons and run screaming, after which Skinner's eyes shift away from the gates.
Skinner commands the flow of the battle like a general.
The skin body is a puppet, and inside is a dark red, eyeless, segmented worm with two antennae and two whip-like tendrils that serve as hands.
Crypt Worms rampage through Antinium tunnels in the Hive and reanimate the Hive's dead.
The Wyvern Lord kills a Garuda [Lieutenant] and crushes a Dullahan [Soldier] when it dives onto Pallass's wall.
A lightning combination from Saliss of Lights leaves a crater in the Wyvern Lord's side, but it is still standing, swaying and stunned.
The Wyvern Lord survives the fight and returns with a much reduced weyr to reclaim territory in the High Passes.
He has killed six challengers within his weyr.
Bird carries and gnaws at a severed Wyvern wing into the inn.
Liscor's dungeon hosts a huge variety of nasty monsters, including Shield Spiders, Crypt Worms, undead, enchanted suits of armor, Bog Wraiths, Face-Eater Moths, giant infested slugs and the Children.
The Antinium also face large maggots that spit acid in the dungeon tunnels.
A dungeon pit trap hides a mile-deep drop with huge webs and gigantic scuttling spiders, including a Shield Spider the size of a house.
Calruz says four great nests in the dungeon are death to awaken: Face-Eater Moths, Shield Spiders, fungus, and one empty because something killed all that was inside.
The fungus nest is sealed off, and Calruz says that if it had a chance to spread it would be deadly, since half the spores shown to him are toxic and some explode.
Natural springs inside the dungeon provide water for its many monsters.
Reports on the dungeon mention infested monsters possibly derived from ancient Drakes and at least one more boss-class guardian monster.
Fierre's family are local farmers whose livestock, such as the sheep Fluffles the Sixth, tend to wander indoors.
